=== Properties ===
==== Weapon ====
{{Feature icon|Ranged}} Strikes targets by aiming and firing at them from a distance.

{{Feature icon|Single Fire}} Fires once when the trigger is pulled. The trigger must be released before firing again.

{{Feature icon|Round Reload}} Inserts a single round on reload. The next round(s) will also start reloading automatically until the magazine is full.

{{Feature icon|Multi-Shot|negative=true}} Releases a single slug projectile with each shot.

{{Feature icon|Aim Down Sights|negative=true}} Cannot use sights. Zooms in slightly instead, but doing so does not significantly affect accuracy.

{{Feature icon|Stable Accuracy|negative=true}} Suffers a significant decrease in accuracy while moving and while airborne.

==== Bullet ====
{{Feature icon|Hitscan}} Up to 25m — Travels in a straight line, meaning there is no bullet drop. The direction will deviate from the crosshairs depending on accuracy.

{{Feature icon|Projectile}} After 25m — Gets affected by gravity and has a travel time.

{{Feature icon|Mid Range Falloff}} Deals reduced damage when hitting targets at a moderate distance (falloff starts at less than 30m).

{{Feature icon|Moderate Structure Damage}} Damages structures. Takes a few seconds or multiple charges to break a concrete wall.

{{Feature icon|Critical Hit|negative=true}} Does not critically hit for increased damage, even if the target was struck on the head. 

{{Feature icon|Interceptible|negative=true}} Can not be removed by the [[APS Turret]].

== Guide ==
=== Strengths ===
* The KS-23 can break through any breakable surface with its slugs, giving the user a way to destroy the enviroment in a few shots without having to rely on charges of explosive [[Gadgets]] like the [[C4]] and [[RPG-7]] or [[Charge 'N' Slam]].
* Dealing up to a 100 damage per shot makes the KS-23 great at dealing quick bursts of high damage while not being reliant on hitting heads, as this weapon has no headshot multiplier.
* Because of it's single-shot nature, the KS-23 is great at dealing poke damage, even at range if the user can predict enemy movement from afar.
* In [[Terminal Attack]], the maximum health Light contestants can regenerate to is 100 health. This is exactly the damage of the KS-23, giving the weapon a slight advantage against that build in the game mode.

=== Weaknesses ===
* Reloading the KS-23's shells takes a long time, leading to significant downtime between firing.
* Having no way to increase the damage per shot, the KS-23 has a slightly longer time-to-kill compared to what other weapons with headshot multipliers of the class can attain. The user may find themselves struggling to defend themselves against weaponry with headshot multipliers, granted that the enemy is hitting headshots (which are the easiest to hit on the class the KS-23 belongs to, considering the [[Heavy|Heavy's]] hitbox size).
* The time-to-kill combined with the KS-23's small magazine size makes missing a shot very punishing.
* The user has to position themselves more mindfully to maintain mid-range distance in order to get the most damage while benefitting from cover during cycling animation downtime.

=== Tactics ===
* The KS-23's hip-fire and ADS accuracy, unlike how other shotguns like the [[SA1216]] or [[Model 1887]] function, is not the same. The user should zoom before firing, significantly decreasing bullet dispersion. 
** While hip-firing is still applicable in close quarters, with the KS23's high time-to-kill, the user should try to minimize the chance of missing if possible.
* Due to the long downtime between firing, it is important for the KS-23 user to utilise cover through the enviroment or [[Gadgets]] in order to hide between shots and mitigate damage taken while the KS-23 cycles its next shot. With the damage starting to fall off at 12 meters, positioning is very important as the user should be trying to find an appropriate distance to their enemies where they can benefit from cover without losing out on too much damage.
** The [[Barricade]] and [[Dome Shield]] are great [[Gadgets]] to pair with the KS-23 to have very quick and durable cover available.
** The [[Goo Gun]] can quickly create a piller of two to three [[Goo]] blobs for similar effect, although less durable and less wide in size.
** The [[Goo Grenade]] creates big walls and is also useful for mobility around the map, but switching to and deploying it takes a decent amount of time and the wall that spawns might not form in a way the user wanted it to.
*** Despite the downtime, the KS-23 is still very capable in direct close range encounters particularly against [[Light|Lights]] and [[Heavy|Heavies]]. The former can be eliminated in just two accurate shots and, when against the latter, the user can substitute the 4th shot with a [[Quick Melee]] attack.
*A quick-melee kick can widen the gap between the user and enemy contestants to force them out of extreme close quarters, if for just a moment, slightly helping with the weapon's downside of being weaker in direct fights.
* A concrete wall and ceilings take two shots to breach, sometimes three if there's additional objects in the way. You can fire slugs until you're one shot away from breaking your obstacle, reload to full then fire the last shot to enter the area with 5/6 shots in your weapon.
* Walls and floors can be prematurely shot with the KS-23 to make them easily breakable later on. This can, for example, be utilized to shoot the ground near the [[Cashout Station]] during defense preparation, to later quickly drop it by shooting the floor when necessary, potentially stalling a steal and preserve charges of explosive [[Gadgets]] if the user has any or somewhat substitute them.
* A KS-23 user may need to lead their target at longer distances, i.e. firing at the location where they will be when the projectile arrives. This is because the KS-23's attack uses a projectile instead of a hitscan beyond 25m.
* A full reload has a long wind-up time, but then reloads much more quickly. For this reason, the full reload should preferably not be interrupted by firing, but the tactical reload can be interrupted.
* Once either reloading animation is started, it can only be cancelled with a [[Quick Melee]] attack until at least one shell has been loaded, after which you can fire at any point, instantly cancelling the animation.
** In a desperate situation, it can be worth to continuously reload a single shot and then shoot the enemy through hip-fire.
*Dealing an immediate 100 damage within effective range, it's important for the user to be aware of certain breakpoints in combination with [[Gadgets]], [[Specializations]], [[Quick Melee]] attacks or even [[Arena Carriables]] so they don't need to rely just on the KS-23's slugs and preserve ammunition.
**A [[Quick Melee]] attack in close range right after a KS-23 hit, dealing 25 damage, can make the difference between winning a fight and losing it or the enemy getting away if they have just a sliver of health left. The KS-23 still needs to cycle its shots however, so the user needs to be aware that they will be stuck in the cycling animation before being able to shoot again. Not being reliant on [[Gadgets]] or [[Specializations]] makes this the most applicable attack to combo with.
**The [[RPG-7]], [[Explosive Mine]], [[C4]] as well as [[Explosive Canister|Explosive Canisters]] can all shave off one shot of the KS-23 time-to-kill.
**The [[Charge 'N' Slam]] deals 100 damage on the initial and 40 damage on subsequent hits. This allows the user substitue KS-23 slugs with initial [[Charge 'N' Slam]] damage in close range. While the combo's could be finished with quick melee attacks, enough chip damage eliminates the need to do so, making them safer to pull off. 
***Even though [[Charge 'N' Slam]] has great combo potential with the KS-23, the user has to be mindful with where they end up after the charge, as they may land in a direct fight with no cover and subsequently be in a disadvantaged position. To help with this, the user should be observant of cover in the vicinity to run to after the charge or outright cancel the charge if they must. If the contestant has it equipped, the [[Barricade]] can be selected during the charge and immediately placed afterwards to create immediate cover.
** The contact damage of thrown [[Arena Carriables]] (with the exception of the [[Explosive Canister]]) and other objects like the [[Vault]] or [[Healing Emitter]] deals between 50 to 75 damage to other contestants, which is enough damage for the KS-23 to require a shot less against any given class depending on their health, saving ammunition. While a niche tactic, this can prove particularly useful when being caught off-guard while carrying the [[Vault]], throwing it at the enemy and following up with the KS-23 instead of simply dropping it first.

== Trivia ==
* The KS-23 exists in real life as the [[Wikipedia:KS-23|KS-23 shotgun]], meaning ''Karabin Spetsialny''—Russian for "Special Carbine". It was designed in the 1970s, under the Soviet Union by [[Wikipedia:TsNIITochMash|TsNIITochMash]] (Tsentral'nyy nauchno-issledovatel'skiy institut tyazhelogo mashinostroyeniya; tr. Central Scientific - Research Institute for Precision Machine Engineering) for the Ministry of Internal Affairs. It was designed with the purpose of suppressing prison riots. It has the capability to fire several different types of ammunition. It is still in service to this day.
** The 23 in KS-23 refers to its 23mm caliber.
** See also: [[List of Gun Origins]].
* After version 6.0.0, the weapon's RPM was only 75 instead of the advertised 85. After version 8.6.0, the weapon's RPM decreased to 73 for unknown reasons. Patch 10.6.0 effectively increases the RPM of the KS-23 to 78.

== Guide ==
===Strengths===
*The Pike-556 is known for its high damage per shot, making it particularly effective at long ranges.
*It benefits from critical hit damage on headshots, rewarding precision and making it lethal in skilled hands.
===Weaknesses===
*The accuracy of the Pike-556 is significantly reduced while moving or airborne, limiting its effectiveness in fast-paced combat scenarios.
===Tactics===
*To maximize accuracy, always aim down sights, especially at longer ranges.
*Prioritize headshots to capitalize on the rifle’s critical hit potential.
*It is advised to remain stationary or crouch to maintain the weapon’s accuracy while firing.
*The Pike-556 has noticeable recoil after each shot. It is recommended to wait for the recoil to reset before firing again to maintain precise shots.

===Properties===
==== Weapon ====
{{Feature icon|Ranged}} Strikes targets by aiming and firing at them from a distance.

{{Feature icon|Single Fire}} Fires once when the trigger is pulled. The trigger must be released before firing again.

{{Feature icon|Aim Down Sights|negative=true}} Cannot use sights. Zooms in slightly (1.5x) instead, doing so allows for better accuracy.

{{Feature icon|Full Reload}} Replaces the entire magazine in one animation on reload.

{{Feature icon|Stable Accuracy|negative=true}} Suffers a significant decrease in accuracy while moving and while airborne.

==== Bullet ====
{{Feature icon|Hitscan}} Travels in a straight line, meaning there is no bullet drop. The direction will deviate from the crosshairs depending on accuracy.

{{Feature icon|Critical Hit}} Critically hits on headshots, applying a damage multiplier.

{{Feature icon|Minor Structure Damage}} Damages structures. Takes a very long time to break a concrete wall.

== Guide==
=== Strengths ===
*High damage and minimal bullet dispersion display the weapon's extreme consistency.
*The .50 Akimbo has a uniquely efficient ratio of reload-time to effective-dps (in comparison to other weapons of the Heavy archetype such as the [[ShAK-50]] and the [[Flamethrower]]).
* Lower damage fall-off than other Heavy weapons allow a .50 Akimbo user to "poke" enemies from far away, even getting long range kills where other Heavy weapons could not. This makes the .50 Akimbo the Heavy archetypes singular effective long range option, making it extremely unique.

=== Weaknesses ===
*The .50 Akimbo can proved difficult for players who haven't spent time with comparable weapons of the other classes (such as the the [[SR-84]], the [[LH1]], or the [[Pike-556]]) due to the precision it demands being a single-shot weapon with a relatively low firerate.
*The .50 Akimbo tends to struggle in close quarters encounters (particularly in the 5-15m range) due the precise single-fire nature of the weapon, as well as the fixed fire rate tempo.

=== Tactics ===
*Pace yourself. It is common practice for contestants using this weapon to opt for slowing down their fire rate to improve their overally accuracy. Playing to the strength of the precise nature of the .50 Akimbo is key: it'll serve the user better landing even just a few hard-hitting "chip" damage shots than attempting to "spray and pray", potentially dealing little-to-no damage.
*Aim for the head! Whenever applicable, it is worth it for the user to further practicing their precision by going for that headshot multiplier.
*Choose your battles. If the user is in a fight that is extremely close range, a user of this weapon should stay on the outskirts of it and see who they can pick off, whenever applicable. Only go within that difficult 5M-to-15M range of enemies when the situation proves the user to have no choice.
*Using the [[Goo Gun]], you can cancel the reload animation of the Akimbo early if you swap to the [[Goo Gun]] then swap back. This is particularly useful for avoiding the last part of the empty clip reload animation (where the deagles cock eachother), as the gun reloads all of its ammo before it plays.

==Trivia ==
*The .50 Akimbo is a dual-wielded pair of the real-world [[Wikipedia:Desert_Eagle|Desert Eagle]], designed by [[Wikipedia:Magnum_Research|Magnum Research]] and [[Wikipedia:Israel_Military_Industries|Israel Military Industries]] in 1979, intended as the self loading pistol meant to replace large caliber revolvers chambering [[Wikipedia:.357_Magnum|.357 Magnum]], [[Wikipedia:.44_Magnum|.44 Magnum]], and [[Wikipedia:.50_Action_Express|.50 Action express]], the caliber designed specially for the Desert Eagle and the caliber the .50 Akimbos chamber ingame

Takes a very long time to break a concrete wall. ==Guide== [[File:Shak_spread.png|thumb|right|300px|
Bullet spread pattern from top view
with approx. head size
]] ===Strengths=== * While the ShAk-50 has a significantly lower magazine capacity than other fully automatic weapons like the [[M60]] and [[Lewis Gun]], it benefits from a shorter tactical and empty reload and less horizontal recoil pattern. * Additionally, while the TTK is similar to those weapons, the individual shot deals considerably higher damage (for instance, landing one headshot with the ShAk-50 deals 50% more damage than with the [[M60]]). ** This also means that being caught with only a handful of bullets left in the current magazine is slightly less detrimental for the ShAk-50. * The ShAk-50 has a relatively tight spread while hip-firing, making it a valid option for fights at short ranges (~ 5m). ===Weaknesses=== * Despite the shorter tactical and empty reload times, due to the low amount of bullets per magazine (being 20), the ShAk-50 sees more frequent downtime, especially in longer fights. * While the individual shot deals considerably higher damage, the shot needs to hit the target in the first place. Missing multiple shots with the ShAk-50 can be very punishing, so it is crucial for the user to have good tracking to make each shot count. * The distance between the two bullets shot by the ShAk-50 upon firing once increases with distance (see graphic on the right). Combined with it's short minimum and maximum range (compared to the [[M60]] and [[Lewis Gun]]), this significantly decreases its effectiveness at longer ranges, as one of the two bullets might not hit the target, halving the damage that this weapon could deal. ===Tactics=== * Since the ShAk-50 can't sustain for long with it's low ammo count, but benefits from a relatively short reload time, it is especially important for the user to be aware of what cover they have readily available to quickly reload during the heat of battle and keep on fighting. ** [[Gadgets]] such as the [[Dome Shield]] or [[Barricade]] can very much help with this if there is not a lot of enviromental cover available. * If the situation allows for it, it is beneficial to utilize the tactical reload of the ShAk-50 instead of emptying the whole magazine, as the tactical reload is almost a full second shorter. * The [[Winch Claw]] is a strong [[Specializations|Specialization]] to be paired with the ShAk-50, as the weapon is at it's most effective close range. Pulling an enemy close and landing a few shots is a quick way to eliminate players and decrease the likelihood of missing shots. {{EquipmentMastery|source1=Damage dealt by the ShAK-50|xp1=0.2 × Damage Dealt|source2=Critical damage dealt by the ShAK-50|xp2=0.2 × Critical Damage Dealt|source3=Opponent eliminated by the ShAK-50|xp3=50|source4=Assist on an opponent damaged by the ShAK-50|xp4=20}} {{EquipmentCosmetics}} ==Trivia== *The ShAK-50 is modeled after the [[Wikipedia:ShAK-12|ShAK-12]], also known as the ASh-12, which is a [[Wikipedia:Bullpup|bullpup]] .50 caliber [[Wikipedia:Battle_Rifle|battle rifle]] designed for close range engagements in urban environments by law enforcement. **Despite functioning as an assault rifle, the ShAK-50 is technically a battle rifle, as the caliber it fires is a [[Wikipedia:Fully_powered_cartridge|full power rifle cartridge]] rather than an [[Wikipedia:Intermediate_cartridge|intermediate rifle cartridge]]. While it can only fire variations of the caliber [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/12.7%C3%9755mm_STs-130#Cartridge_variants_for_use_in_the_ShAK-12_assault_rifle designated for its use], which are significantly shorter, lower power, and lower grain than the primary variants designed originally for the [[Wikipedia:VKS_Vykhlop|VKS Sniper Rifle]]. The BFR Titan reloads by inserting one round at a time, making its reload very slow. However, the reload can be interrupted before the magazine is full to reload less rounds.

==Guide==

=== General Guide ===
The BFR Titan can be thought of as Heavy's version of the [[CB-01 Repeater]] with good range and great single shot damage. The BFR works better at long range due to its slightly higher base damage (90 vs. 84) and damage fall off multiplier (0.7 vs. 0.64) allowing the user to still meaningfully contribute to fights so long as they have a sight line and the skill to hit long range shots. The one disadvantage of this gun compared to the CB-01 is its lack of ammo (5 vs. 8 rounds) and a speed loader. However, this simply requires the user to take advantage of the segmented reload that the BFR provides by consistently reloading outside of combat.

=== Alternatives to the BFR Titan ===
While it is fun to carry the biggest iron in the arena, and it thrives in long-range arenas such as [[Monaco]], [[SYS$HORIZON]], and [[Kyoto]] in certain shorter-range urban arenas such as [[Bernal]] and [[Las Vegas|New Vegas]], it is recommended to utilize shorter-range weapons or weapons with more utility such as [[KS-23]], [[.50 Akimbo]], or even [[Sledgehammer]] should the user have the requisite skill with it.

The [[Breach Charge]] is a [[Light]] class mounted gadget which, when remotely detonated, creates an explosion that breaches structures.

== Usage ==
The Breach Charge can be selected as one of three [[Gadgets|gadgets]] of any [[Light]] build loadout.

The primary trigger can be used to toss the gadget a small distance. It will attach to the first surface it contacts. 

Once the gadget is armed, the user can use the gadget's secondary trigger to detonate the explosive remotely, from any place at any time.

The gadget can also be retrieved to restore a charge, by interacting with it for a few moments while looking at it from up close.

=== Detonator ===
*When armed, the light on the detonator is blue. 
*When disarmed, the light on the detonator is yellow. 
*When no breach charges are deployed, the light is red.

{{Control scheme|gadget=Equip [[Breach Charge]]|primary-fire=Toss <small>(Tap)</small>|secondary-fire=Detonate <small>(Tap)</small>|interact=Retrieve deployed Breach Charge <small>(Hold)</small>}}
== Stats ==
=== Effects ===
The Breach Charge can be deployed with a small throw to attach it to a nearby surface. The gadget will arm itself after a few moments. From this point on, it can be remotely detonated, causing it to explode. The explosion deals major damage to the surrounding structure, effectively creating a large hole, and also deals damage to opponents in a small area.

If an opponent destroys the gadget, they become the user instead, meaning any damage it deals is attributed to them.

=== Properties ===
==== Gadget ====
{{Feature icon|Tossed}} Can be thrown out a short distance, after which it attaches to the first surface it hits.

{{Feature icon|Single Charge}} Can be used once, then recharges automatically over the cooldown time.

{{Feature icon|Retrievable}} Can be picked up after being deployed to restore a charge.

{{Feature icon|Remote Controlled}} Comes with a remote to trigger all deployed Breach Charges from any distance.

{{Feature icon|Deployment Limit}} 3 Breach Charges can be deployed at a time. An excess deployment causes the oldest Breach Charge to disappear.

==== Projectile ====
{{Feature icon|Projectile}} Gets affected by gravity and has a travel time. Once attached, the gadget is no longer a projectile.

{{Feature icon|Interceptible}} While not attached, can be removed by the [[APS Turret]], nullifying its effects. This causes the turret to lose some health.

{{Feature icon|Trigger on Impact|negative=true}} Does not trigger when thrown at a contestant, instead flies through them.

{{Feature icon|Damaging|negative=true}} Hitting a contestant directly with the projectile does not deal damage.

==== Charge ====
{{Feature icon|Attached}} Attaches to a surface upon deployment. Sticks to the surface even if it moves. Weighs down any [[Arena Carriables|carriable object]] it is attached to.

{{Feature icon|Solid}} Has its own collision, albeit of a very small size, that can be stood upon.

{{Feature icon|Arming Time}} Disarmed when initially deployed or while picked up as an attachment. Arms automatically after a wind-up time.

{{Feature icon|Destructible}} Can be destroyed if its health is fully depleted, such as through hits from bullets or explosions. This causes the Breach Charge to explode. Teammates can also destroy it.

{{Feature icon|Glitchable}} Can be temporarily disabled by a [[Glitch Grenade]] or [[Glitch Barrel]].

{{Feature icon|Reshapeable}} Can be reshaped by the [[Data Reshaper]] into a piece of [[Arena Carriables|decor]] by opponents.

{{Feature icon|Sound Cue}} Produces a constant beeping noise while it is armed, alerting nearby contestants of its presence.

{{Feature icon|Permanent}} Does not disappear by itself.

{{Feature icon|Reversible}} Can be used against the user's team, if an opponent triggers the explosion by destroying the gadget. Any damage and eliminations are attributed to the opponent.

==== Explosion ====
{{Feature icon|Explosive}} Deals damage in an area of effect that can be intercepted by structures and shields.

{{Feature icon|Damaging}} Deals damage to contestants.

{{Feature icon|Major Structure Damage}} Damages structures. Instantly destroys a concrete wall.

{{Feature icon|Friendly Fire|negative=true}} Can damage the user, but not their teammates (unless an opponent caused it to explode).

== Guide ==
==== Strengths ====
* Compared to the similar [[Thermal Bore]], the Breach Charge can be used more frequently and can be detonated at a later point, even while not near the line of sight of the breaching point.
* The Breach Charge can create shortcuts through buildings, which is especially useful on arenas such as [[Las Vegas]] and [[SYS$HORIZON]] where the interiors can be quite mazelike.

==== Weaknesses ====
* The Breach Charge can be disabled by a nearby [[Glitch Grenade]] or [[Glitch Barrel]] triggering, or reshaped by the [[Data Reshaper]].

==== Tactics ====
* The Breach Charge can be used in tandem with [[Arena Carriables|arena carriables]] to create anything from deadly bombs with the Oil Barrels and [[Explosive Canister|Explosive Canisters]], to on-demand cover with the [[Goo Barrel]].
* The Breach Charge has a very niche use with the Goo Grenade, allowing for a clever strategy of blowing a hole through a wall and deploying [[Goo]] to create a platform to shoot through the hole. This will create an unexpected sightline and allow the user to catch enemies off guard.
*Placing a breach charge next to a [[Zipline]] can be used to remotely send opponents falling to their deaths.
*3 stacked breach charges deal enough damage to eliminate [[light]] contestants. This can be employed to instantly prevent contestants from completing objectives.

Reload - 1.9s |ammo=1 |duration=3.75s |maxrange=16m }} The '''Nullifier''' is a [[Light]] class gadget that can zap a contestant to nullify them. {{Infographic | infographic-class = right | display = image | Image = mov_l_nullifier.gif }} == Usage == The Nullifier can be selected as one of three [[Gadgets|gadgets]] of any [[Light]] build loadout. The gadget can be held and fired like a weapon. The gadget has stable accuracy even while moving. Aiming down sights is possible but will not increase accuracy. The trigger can be pulled to fire an electric pulse that will nullify the first opponent it hits. When a new charge of the Nullifier is ready, it needs to be reloaded like a weapon, unlike most gadgets. The reloading animation is automatically started once a charge is ready and the gadget is held. {{Control scheme|gadget=Equip [[Nullifier]]|secondary-fire=Aim down sights (Hold)}} == Stats == === Effects === The Nullifier can be deployed by firing it from a short distance. If the electric pulse hits a contestant, they become nullified for a short duration. While nullified, the affected contestant becomes transparent and cannot receive damage until the effect ends. Similarly, they cannot block hitscan bullets for teammates, but can block projectiles. As the effect nears its end, the contestant emits an escalating audio cue and gradually brightens, signaling that the nullification is about to expire. Nullified contestants can still move normally and reload their [[Weapons|Weapon]], but they are unable to perform the following actions: * Fire or otherwise use their [[Weapons|Weapon]] * Use any equipped [[Gadgets]] or their [[Specializations|Specialization]] ** Gadgets that require reloading, such as the [[RPG-7]], also cannot be reloaded * Perform most actions requiring the '''Interact''' keybind, including but not limited to opening [[Vault|Vaults]], stealing a [[Cashout Station]], moving through [[Gateway|Gateways]], or reviving contestants ** Any interaction already in progress is immediately interrupted when the Nullifier effect is applied * Grab onto a [[Zipline]], though any active zipline ride will not be interrupted * Emote, play a sound, or use a spray While nullified contestants are immune to all forms of damage, they are still affected by certain movement-impairing effects, such as the pull of a [[Gravity Vortex]] or the lift from an [[Anti-Gravity Cube]]. === Properties === ==== Gadget ==== {{Feature icon|Ranged}} Strikes targets by aiming and firing at them from a distance. {{Feature icon|Aim Down Sights}} Has iron sights that significantly increase accuracy when used. {{Feature icon|Scope}} Has the ability to aim down sights, though this does not significantly affect accuracy. Iron sights replace the crosshairs. {{Feature icon|Stable Accuracy}} Keeps a stable accuracy, even while moving and going airborne. {{Feature icon|Single Charge}} Can be used once, then recharges automatically over the cooldown time. {{Feature icon|Gadget Reload}} Automatically goes into a reloading animation once the gadget is used and a new charge is ready to be loaded. ==== Zap ==== {{Feature icon|Hitscan}} Travels in a straight line. {{Feature icon|Trigger on Impact}} Applies its effects if an opponent is struck. {{Feature icon|Interceptible|negative=true}} Can not be removed by the [[APS Turret]]. {{Feature icon|Damaging|negative=true}} Hitting a contestant directly with the projectile does not deal damage. ==== Effect ==== {{Feature icon|Glitching|negative=true}} Does not glitch affected contestants, but the Nullifier will prevent the use of [[Specializations|specializations]] and interrupts actions such as stealing a cashout. {{Feature icon|Disabling|negative=true}} Does not disable glitchable gadgets. {{Feature icon|Friendly Fire|negative=true}} Can affect neither the user nor their teammates. == Guide == === Strengths === * Hitting a contestant with the Nullifier instantly stops any ongoing interactions, including a revive in progress or [[Cashout Station]] steal. * Nullified contestants are effectively removed from the fight until the effect expires; their only viable actions are repositioning. Since they cannot use their [[Gadgets]] or [[Specializations|Specialization]], it can create an opening to exploit. * Hitting a nullified opponent with a precise strike rewards stamina. === Weaknesses === * Requires accuracy to administer. Like most [[Gadgets]], the charge is consumed even if the user misses. * Using the Nullifier on an incorrect contestant or with bad timing can lead to missed opportunities, such as nullifying a contestant who's elimination is already imminent. ** This can easily allow the target to run or escape, since they cannot receive damage while nullified. {{EquipmentMastery|source1=Firing the Nullifier|xp1=0|source2=Striking an opponent with the Nullifier|xp2=200|source3=Assisting with elimination of opponent by shooting them with the Nullifier|xp3=75}} {{EquipmentCosmetics}} ==Trivia== *The Nullifier takes visual inspiration from the Axon Enterprise [[Media:Zapinator.jpg|Taser 7]]. == History == {| class="wikitable" !Patch !!

}}{{Removed|perm=yes}}'''Recon Senses''' was a [[Medium|Medium Build]] specialization. It was significantly reworked into a [[Light]] [[gadgets|gadget]] - [[Thermal Vision]], that later became a [[True Sight]] [[Specializations|specialization]]. Reworked ability works significantly different from the original, not offering vision through obstacles.

== Overview ==
Recon Senses is an optical enhancement that enhances visibility and reveals the positions of enemy contestants. The maximum amount of time that this ability can be active is 8.25 seconds. The ability recharge takes twice the time that it was active; i.e. it would take 10 seconds to recharge after being used for 5 seconds. However, it can be used while recharging, as long as it has around a fifth of it's charge available. 

== Interactions ==

* Using Recon Senses highlights enemies in a faint red color, allowing you to see them through structures, foliage, and smoke.
* The activation cost is 1.5 seconds.
* The minimum charge time to activate is 2 seconds.
* The highlight effect weakens as distance increases.
* While Recon Senses are active, players within it's range will have the word "Detected"  displayed on their screen, similar to [[Sonar Grenade|Sonar Grenades]].

== Strengths and Weaknesses ==

* This specialization can give players a tactical advantage by allowing them to track the movements of enemies and plan their attack or defense accordingly. It is most effective when used in combination with good communication and teamwork. 
* When facing Light players using a [[Cloaking Device]], Recon Senses can provide early warning and has the potential to completely shut down their ambush capabilities, especially if they are also using a [[SH1900]] shotgun as they would be unprepared to respond to suddenly being fired upon from outside their effective range. 
* Players who are not able to communicate with their team will not be able to share the location of highlighted enemies through structures, which means this specialization may not be as beneficial to the team as the [[Healing Beam]] or [[Guardian Turret]]. This specialization's long cooldown means the user must be able to manage its usage efficiently.

== Usage ==
The Goo Gun can be selected as the [[Specializations|specialization]] gadget of any [[Heavy]] build loadout.

The Goo Gun is very versatile, Its prime uses are for creating defenses, blocking turrets, mines and grenades, and being used as a movement tool.

Additionally it has more obscure uses such as: Temporarily trapping enemies to close gaps or run away, Quickly destroying APS turrets, Interrupting steals and revives, Moving cashout stations, and more.

The Goo Gun rewards out of the box thinking and fast reactions, every use has a time and place.
{{Control scheme|specialization=Equip [[Goo Gun]]|primary-fire=Fire goo <small>(Tap)</small>|reload=Tactical reload}}
== Stats ==
=== Effects ===
The Goo Gun can be used to create blobs of [[goo]]. The goo will stick to the first entity it hits; besides surfaces, this can be another piece of goo, an [[Arena Carriables|arena carriable]] or a contestant.

The goo can be damaged by opponents and teammates to destroy it. The created goo is also highly flammable; a nearby fire will quickly spread to any connected pieces of goo and destroy it after a few seconds.

If a goo piece is fired at a contestant, they will be momentarily slowed before the goo destroys itself. This also interrupts any action the contestant is currently performing, including reviving or stealing cashouts.
=== Properties ===
==== Gadget ====
{{Feature icon|Ranged}} Strikes targets by aiming and firing at them from a distance.

{{Feature icon|Stable Accuracy}} Keeps a stable accuracy, even while moving and going airborne.

{{Feature icon|Full Reload}} Replaces the entire magazine in one animation on reload.

{{Feature icon|Deployment Limit|negative=true}} Can be deployed any number of times.

==== Projectile ====
{{Feature icon|Projectile}} Gets affected by gravity and has a travel time. Once attached, the gadget is no longer a projectile.

{{Feature icon|Trigger on Impact}} Can fly for any amount of time and triggers when the projectile collides with a surface or contestant, creating a Placed Goo.

{{Feature icon|Interceptible}} Can be removed by the [[APS Turret]], nullifying its effects. This causes the turret to lose some health.

{{Feature icon|Damaging|negative=true}} Hitting a contestant directly with the projectile does not deal damage.

{{Feature icon|Destructible|negative=true}} Cannot be destroyed by receiving damage such as from bullets or explosions.

==== Goo ====
{{Feature icon|Attached}} Attaches to a surface upon deployment. Sticks to the surface even if it moves. Weighs down any [[Arena Carriables|carriable object]] it is attached to.

{{Feature icon|Solid}} Has its own collision, meaning it blocks bullets and contestants can stand on it.

{{Feature icon|Destructible}} Can be destroyed if its health is fully depleted, such as through hits from bullets or explosions. Teammates can also destroy it.

{{Feature icon|Immobilizing}} Can trap contestants, making them unable to move until the goo destroys itself a moment later.

{{Feature icon|Reshapeable|negative=true}} Cannot be reshaped by the [[Data Reshaper]].

{{Feature icon|Permanent|negative=true}} Disappears by itself after enough time has passed.

== Guide ==
=== Strengths ===
* The Goo Gun can block off potential all the entry points of an area, such as windows.
* The Goo Gun can be used to briefly incapacitate players by trapping them in a blob of goo.
* Goo placed by the Goo Gun can be used to access inaccessible areas, or open up alternative entry points.

=== Weaknesses ===
* [[Fire]] can get rid of constructions made by the Goo Gun.

=== Tactics ===
* The Goo Gun is an integral part of making a flying machine, by attaching a goo construction to a detached [[Barricade]] and throwing an [[Anti-Gravity Cube]] to move the Barricade up, and by extension, the goo construction that is holding the Anti-Gravity Cube and the user.
* The Goo Gun can be used to surround an objective in a wall of goo, often called a "cocoon." Paired with an [[Anti-Gravity Cube]], they can be attached to walls or ceilings, making them much harder to bypass.
* The Goo Gun can quickly destroy an [[APS Turret]] by firing multiple shots near it, as each blob is intercepted and damages the turret.

It was disabled since [[Season 8]] and was finally reworked in [[Season 12]] into [[True Sight]] specialization. {{Infographic | infographic-class = right | display = image | Image = mov_l_thermalvision.gif }} == Usage == Thermal Vision can be selected as one of three [[Gadgets|gadgets]] of any [[Light]] build loadout. The primary trigger can be used to toggle on the gadget. It will remain active even while not holding the item for up to 30 seconds, after which it is automatically disabled to recharge. It can also be disabled before this point by toggling it again. {{Control scheme|gadget=Equip [[Thermal Vision]]|primary-fire=Toggle on (Tap)
Toggle off (Tap)}} == Stats == === Effects === Thermal Vision can be activated to grant its user temporary thermal vision. Most of the screen will be a gray color, whereas significant objects are highlighted in white. These objects include contestants, [[Arena Carriables|barrels]], [[Cash Box|cash boxes]] and a few others. It also allows its user to see past vision-obstructing objects, such as [[Smoke Grenade|smoke clouds]] and [[Gas|gas clouds]], but also general dust and debris caused by destruction and explosions, making for a clearer view of the area. Opponents are fully visible even if they are under the effects of the [[Cloaking Device]] or [[Vanishing Bomb]]. If opponents are a long distance away, though, or fully obscured by a [[Smoke Grenade|smoke cloud]], they will not be highlighted during Thermal Vision and will simply be gray. === Properties === ==== Gadget ==== {{Feature icon|Self Targeted}} Can be activated to apply an effect to the contestant that used it. {{Feature icon|Toggle}} Can be enabled and disabled by reactivating. {{Feature icon|Single Charge}} Can be used once, then recharges automatically over the cooldown time. {{Feature icon|Disarms User|negative=true}} Does not stop the user from using their other items while the gadget is active. ==== Effect ==== {{Feature icon|Visibility}} Affects the line of sight of the user and/or opponents. Changes the user's viewing mode to thermal vision. {{Feature icon|Permanent|negative=true}} Disappears by itself after enough time has passed. == Guide == === Strengths === * Thermal Vision is an effective counter to [[Light]] contestants using the [[Cloaking Device]], as it will reveal them to the Thermal Vision user. * Thermal Vision has very short downtimes compared to its maximum duration. * In confined areas with lots of explosions, dust clouds and other vision-obstructing particles, Thermal Vision often provides the most value. === Weaknesses === * Thermal Vision cannot see [[gas]], which can potentially cause the user to walk into a damaging area unintentionally. * Thermal Vision has limited range and will not highlight far-away opponents. * When an opponent is not considered to be in the user's line of sight, they will not be highlighted. This includes them being fully obscured by a [[Smoke Grenade|smoke cloud]], even though the user can see through it with the gadget. In this case, the opponent will be grayscale and blends into the environment. === Tactics === * Thermal Vision can be combined with the [[Smoke Grenade]], as it is able to see through the smoke. == Item Mastery == Item mastery XP for the {{{1|{{PAGENAME}}}}} can be earned by actively using it. {| class="wikitable" |- |colspan="2" |'''

{{Infobox gadgets |image=Gateway.png |name=GATEWAY |quote={{quote|text=A pair of deployable gateway entrances; when both are placed and activated, contestants and objects can move between the two locations}} |build=Light |type=Utility |unlock=500 |cooldown=50s |ammo=2 |duration=20s |maxrange=60m }} The [[Gateway]] is a [[Light]] class thrown gadget that creates two portals between which contestants and objects can teleport. {{Infographic | infographic-class = right | display = image | Image = mov_l_gateway.gif }} == Usage == The Gateway can be selected as one of three [[Gadgets|gadgets]] of any [[Light]] build loadout. Holding the primary trigger will prepare a high-velocity overhand throw. Holding the secondary trigger will prepare a low-velocity underhand throw. While preparing a throw, the gadget's trajectory is indicated up to the point where it bounces off a surface (or up to its mid-air detonation point). Swapping to a different item will cancel the throw. Releasing the trigger throws the gadget. Throwing a second gateway will connect it to the first. To enter a gateway, any contestant can interact with one of the gateways to travel to the other. Alternatively, projectiles and objects can be thrown into the gateway to teleport them on their own. {{Control scheme|gadget=Equip [[Gateway]]|primary-fire=Prepare overhand throw (Hold)
Overhand Throw (Release)|secondary-fire=Prepare underhand throw (Hold)
Underhand Throw (Release)|interact=Enter connected Gateway (Tap)}} == Stats == === Effects === The Gateway can be deployed by throwing it. A few seconds after being deployed, it creates a closed gateway. The same process is repeated for the second deployment, at which point the two gateways connect. Contestants (including opponents) can use the gateway to travel to the other gateway (with a cooldown of 3 seconds) until it disappears after 20 seconds. Additionally, any objects (such as the [[Frag Grenade]] or a [[Arena Carriables|barrel]]) are also teleported if they come into a gateway's proximity. === Properties === ==== Gadget ==== {{Feature icon|Grenade}} Can be thrown like a grenade, meaning overhand or underhand. The trajectory and explosion point are shown as an indicator. {{Feature icon|Multiple Charges}} Has 2 charges, but both need to be used to create a gateway. Recharging starts when both charges are used and restores both charges at once. ==== Projectile ==== {{Feature icon|Projectile}} Gets affected by gravity and has a travel time. {{Feature icon|Bounce}} Bounces away when the projectile collides with a surface or contestant. {{Feature icon|Trigger on Time}} Triggers after a fixed amount of time, regardless of whether the projectile has struck opponents or surfaces. {{Feature icon|Interceptible}} Can be removed by the [[APS Turret]], nullifying its effects. This causes the turret to lose some health. {{Feature icon|Reshapeable}} Can be reshaped by the [[Data Reshaper]] into a piece of [[Arena Carriables|decor]] by opponents. ==== Gateway ==== {{Feature icon|Glitchable}} Can be temporarily disabled by a [[Glitch Grenade]] or [[Glitch Barrel]]. {{Feature icon|Usable by Opponents}} Can be used by opponents to their advantage. {{Feature icon|Movement}} Provides a special mode of transport for contestants. Also teleports projectiles and objects that go near the gateway. {{Feature icon|Reshapeable}} Can be reshaped by the [[Data Reshaper]], closing both ends of the gateway. {{Feature icon|Attached|negative=true}} Does not attach to a surface upon deployment. {{Feature icon|Destructible|negative=true}} Cannot be destroyed by receiving damage such as from bullets or explosions. == Guide == === Strengths === * A gateway can be held unopened for as long as needed. The duration begins only when the second gateway is placed. === Weaknesses === * Opponents can follow the user through their gateway. === Tactics === * A gateway can be made to detonate in mid-air, so that it becomes a one-way portal as contestants would not be able to reach it. * By activating a gateway with one portal on a vault, the cash box from said vault can automatically be teleported as soon as the vault unlocks. This is often useful to bypass teams that might be contesting the vault or to gain a tempo advantage by quickly activating a cashout station. * An inactive portal is deployed indefinitely as long as the user stays within its 60m range. Hence a portal can be placed down before entering a fight, and returned to very quickly by deploying the second portal and entering the gateway. This trick can be used to get out of sticky situations or to quickly change position and surprise an enemy. * A gateway can be used to quickly reposition an entire team, whether that be to a strategic position or simply out of a sticky situation. * Mines, barrels, and other projectiles such as RPGs can be transported through the gateway, letting contestants eliminate opponents remotely. {{EquipmentMastery|source1=Deploying a Gateway|xp1=25|source2=Contestant travelled through the Gateway|xp2=25 per contestant|source3=Item travelled through the Gateway|xp3=0}} {{EquipmentCosmetics}} == History == {| class="wikitable" !Patch !!

The [[Dematerializer]] is a [[Medium]] class specialization that temporarily removes surfaces, allowing contestants to move and attack through them.
{{Infographic | infographic-class = right | display = image
 | Image = Mov_m_dematerializer.gif
}} 
== Usage ==

The Dematerializer can be selected as the [[Specializations|specialization]] gadget of any [[Medium]] build loadout.

While the gadget is held, looking at a surface will show an indicator of a potential dematerialization as a blue hologram covering a part of the surface. The primary trigger can be used to activate the gadget and dematerialize the surface. 

If a surface was already dematerialized by any contestant, the indicator will be red instead, and the secondary trigger can be used to rematerialize the surface.
{{Control scheme|specialization=Equip [[Dematerializer]]|primary-fire=Dematerialize surface <small>(Tap)</small>|secondary-fire=Rematerialize surface <small>(Tap)</small>}}
== Stats ==
=== Effects ===
The Dematerializer can be deployed by activating it on a targeted surface. This will cause the surface to turn into its dematerialized version. Contestants, attacks and other objects can look and phase through the wall freely. The Dematerializer will remove props attached to wall segments. 

After a while, the surface rematerializes automatically, or it can be rematerialized manually.

=== Properties ===
==== Gadget ====
{{Feature icon|Targeted}} Can be activated while targeting a structure piece or solid object.

{{Feature icon|Toggle}} Can be enabled and disabled by reactivating. Specifically, a dematerialized surface will rematerialize if it is reactivated.

{{Feature icon|Multiple Charges}} Can be used 2 times. When a charge is used, it automatically recharges over the cooldown time.

{{Feature icon|Deployment Limit|negative=true}} Any number of walls can be dematerialized at a time.

==== Dematerialized Surface ====
{{Feature icon|Attached}} Attached to a structure piece or solid object.

{{Feature icon|Sound Cue}} Produces a sound to alert nearby contestants when used. A dematerialized surface also hums softly.

{{Feature icon|Usable by Opponents}} Can be used by opponents to their advantage. Opponents can see, shoot and move through the gaps.

{{Feature icon|Permanent|negative=true}} Disappears by itself after enough time has passed.

{{Feature icon|Damaging|negative=true}} Does not inflict damage.

{{Feature icon|Minor Structure Damage|negative=true}} Instantly removes a surface of any structure. However, this does not affect the structural integrity of the surrounding structure, and the removal is reversed after some time, or upon reactivation.

== Guide ==
=== Strengths ===
* The Dematerializer can be used to create unexpected angles and opportunities while also being able to close the hole to deny opponents the possibility of retaliation.

=== Weaknesses ===
* If the surfaces around an objective are already breached in several places such as by [[Arena_Carriables|Explosive Canisters]], a Dematerializer user will not get as much benefit from the gadget, as opponents can easily follow them.
* It can be difficult to see well through a dematerialized surface to fire through it, due to the glitchy animation overlay, especially if opponents are far away from the surface.
* When the user is playing in an uncoordinated team, the Dematerializer may only benefit its user, whereas the other Medium [[Specializations]] would also benefit the team. However, with proper communication, the Dematerializer can be used strategically by the entire team. Additionally, capturing objectives using the Dematerializer also benefits the team regardless.

=== Tactics ===
* It is possible to defend an objective from an adjacent room, besides or above the room the station is in, by opening a hole whenever the sound cue plays and taking down the opponent while they are attempting to steal.
* To escape from a sticky situation, the user can dematerialize the floor under them or a wall besides them and rematerialize immediately after going through. 
** However, it should be noted that there can sometimes be additional obstacles in unpredictable locations that block the way through, such as a cabinet behind a wall or a pipeline on a ceiling which may require an additional dematerialization. This happens particularly often on [[Las Vegas]] and [[Horizon]].
* The Dematerializer can be used to take the [[Cashout Station]] down a floor and immediately rematerialize the opened ceiling, allowing for a quick steal. 
** Alternatively, if the station is placed against a wall, dematerializing a cell in the wall may allow for an unexpected steal from behind while the rest of the wall and the station itself provides cover for the stealer. 
** These strategies also apply to encrypting or decrypting [[Terminal Attack]]'s terminal.

The gadget will arm itself after a few moments. From this point on, it can be remotely activated, causing the Gravity Vortex to appear. The Vortex pulls surrounding objects, like Cashout Stations, Contestants and [[Arena Carriables]], to its center, effectively creating a difficult to traverse area. === Properties === ==== Gadget ==== {{feature icon|Gadget}} Used by the contestant as an offensive, defensive or utility tool, and automatically recharges after being used. {{Feature icon|Tossed}} Can be thrown out a short distance, after which it attaches to the first surface it hits. {{Feature icon|Single Charge}} Can be used once, then recharges automatically over the cooldown time. {{Feature icon|Retrievable}} Can be picked up after being deployed to restore a charge. {{feature icon|Remote Controlled}} Can be activated remotely once deployed and armed. {{Feature icon|Deployment Limit}} 1 Gravity Vortex can be deployed at a time. Only expires once activated. ==== Gravity Vortex ==== {{feature icon|Attached}} Attaches to a surface upon deployment, sticking to that surface even if it moves. Can be attached to [[Arena Carriables|carriable objects]] to add weight to them. {{feature icon|Immobilizing}} Pulls in nearby contestants and loose objects. Can be escaped by moving away from the center for a brief period. {{feature icon|Glitchable}} Can be destroyed by a [[Glitch Grenade]] or [[Glitch Barrel]]; Glitch Grenades detonate immediately on impact. {{feature icon|Friendly Fire}} Can pull in the user and their teammates if they approach the vortex once it is activated. {{feature icon|Limited Duration}} Lasts for a limited time once activated. {{feature icon|Damaging|negative=true}} Does not directly deal damage. == Guide == === Strengths === * The Gravity Vortex is effective at locking down an area via crowd control, forcing any contestants nearby the gadget once it is activated to have their movement temporarily restrained until they can escape. * Easily creates openings; contestants trapped in the vortex cannot move quickly. The [[Shockwave]] is a [[Medium]] class specialization that creates orbs which detonate on impact, pushing players and objects away from the blast with force. These orbs detach mines and turrets, and disrupt and displace opponents.
{{Infographic | infographic-class = right | display = image
 | Image = Mov_m_shockwave.gif
}}
== Usage ==

The Shockwave can be selected as the [[Specializations|specialization]] gadget of any [[Medium]] build loadout. 

When the Specialization key is tapped, the user will summon a Shockwave in their left hand and then proceed to launch it forwards at where their crosshair is placed. 

When the Specialization key is held, the user will still summon a Shockwave, however will continue holding it until releasing the Specialization key or being interrupted. Holding the Specialization key does not increase the radius or the strength of the Shockwave, however releasing a held Shockwave is slightly faster than summoning then launching a Shockwave. 

{{Control scheme|specialization=Equip [[Shockwave]]}}
== Stats ==
=== Effects ===
The Shockwave projectile will explode on impact of any surface, and when it does it will release an equal amount of force from the point of impact within it's entire radius, knocking away the user, opponents, [[Arena Carriables]], the [[Cashout Station]], and detach [[:Category:Sticky Gadgets|Sticky Gadgets]] before also knocking them away. The Shockwave will ignore teammates. 

The Shockwave will also do minor amounts of environmental damage, enough to break glass and windows. 

The Shockwave also disrupts opponents, forcing them to drop any Arena Carriables they were holding, and knock them off [[Zipline|Ziplines]] and [[Ladders]]. The Shockwave does not directly interrupt opponents from held interactions such as revivng and stealing Cashout Stations; however, the knockback from the Shockwave will often create enough distance between opponents and the object they are interacting that it still works to interrupt the interaction. 

The shockwave applies a glitch effect to any opponents, that it hits, disabling gadgets and specialisations, but leaving deployables such as [[Guardian Turret]], active. 

=== Properties ===
==== Specialization ====
{{Feature icon|Ranged}} Strikes targets by aiming and firing at them from a distance.

{{Feature icon|Stable Accuracy}} Keeps a stable accuracy, even while moving and going airborne.

{{Feature icon|Multiple Charges}} Can be used 2 times. When a charge is used, it automatically recharges over the cooldown time.

{{Feature icon|Disarms User|negative=true}} Does not stop the user from using their other items while the gadget is active.

==== Orb ====
{{Feature icon|Projectile}} Has a travel time. Is not affected by gravity.

{{Feature icon|Trigger on Impact}} Can fly for any amount of time and triggers when the projectile collides with a surface or contestant.

{{Feature icon|Glitching}} Glitches affected contestants, making them unable to use gadgets and specialisations, as well as obfuscating their HUD.

{{Feature icon|Minor Structure Damage}} Deals minor structural damage, enough to break windows and glass. 

{{Feature icon|Damaging|negative=true}} Hitting a contestant directly with the projectile does not deal damage, only pushes them.

{{Feature icon|Friendly Fire|negative=true}} Can affect user, but not their teammates.

== Guide ==
=== Strengths ===
* The Shockwave gives the medium much higher mobility, allowing users to more easily rollout or escape danger. 
* The Shockwave's knockback can be used for a variety of purposes, such as knocking away opponents stealing a cashout or off a cliff, knocking a cash box out of an opponent's hand, or knocking a teammate's statue towards the user.
*As the glitch effect travels through shields, throwing a shockwave at opponents using [[Mesh Shield]] will disabke the shield and leave them vulnerable. 


=== Weaknesses ===
* Unlike other Medium specializations, the Shockwave does not provide much teamwide utility like the [[Dematerializer]] or the [[Healing Beam]]. 
* The Shockwave struggles indoors as low ceilings and walls limit the mobility of Shockwave users.

=== Tactics ===
* Launch a Shockwave right before stepping on a [[Jump Pad]] or [[Gameplay#Environment|Triangle Pad]] to combine the push force of both and achieve greater vertical height. 
* Landing a Shockwave so that it cancels an opponent's horizontal velocity will knock up opponents. This tactic is called juggling and can be used to close the distance between the Shockwave user and their opponents, which is especially useful for melee weapons such as the [[Riot Shield]].

{{Infobox gadgets |image=C4_charge.png |name=C4 |quote={{Quote|text=Highly destructive deployable explosive that can be remotely detonated}} |build=Heavy |type=Offensive |unlock=Strategist |cooldown=45s |ammo=1 |damage=155 |dmgradius=Inner - 1.6m
Outer - 6.5m |health=25 |maxdeploy=2 |primetime=1.9s |envdmg=Over 2000}} The [[C4]] is a [[Heavy]] class mounted gadget which, when remotely detonated, creates an explosion that deals high damage and breaches structures. == Usage == The C4 can be selected as one of three [[Gadgets|gadgets]] of any [[Heavy]] build loadout. The primary trigger can be used to toss the gadget a small distance. It will attach to the first surface it contacts. Once the gadget is armed, the user can use the gadget's secondary trigger to detonate the explosive remotely, from any place at any time. The gadget can also be retrieved to restore a charge, by interacting with it for a few moments while looking at it from up close. == Detonator == *When armed, the light on the detonator is blue. *When disarmed, the light on the detonator is yellow. *When no C4 is deployed, the light is red. {{Control scheme|gadget=Equip [[C4]]|primary-fire=Toss (Tap)|secondary-fire=Detonate (Tap)|interact=Retrieve deployed C4 (Hold)}} == Stats == === Effects === The C4 can be deployed with a small throw to attach it to a nearby surface. The gadget will arm itself after a few moments. From this point on, it can be remotely detonated, causing it to explode. The explosion deals high damage to opponents in a large area and major damage to the surrounding structure, effectively creating a large hole. If an opponent destroys the gadget, they become the user instead, meaning any damage it deals is attributed to them. === Properties === ==== Gadget ==== {{Feature icon|Tossed}} Can be thrown out a short distance, after which it attaches to the first surface it hits. {{Feature icon|Single Charge}} Can be used once, then recharges automatically over the cooldown time. {{Feature icon|Retrievable}} Can be picked up after being deployed to restore a charge. {{Feature icon|Remote Controlled}} Comes with a remote to trigger all deployed C4s from any distance. {{Feature icon|Deployment Limit}} 2 C4s can be deployed at a time. An excess deployment causes the oldest C4 to disappear. ==== Projectile ==== {{Feature icon|Projectile}} Gets affected by gravity and has a travel time. Once attached, the gadget is no longer a projectile. {{Feature icon|Interceptible}} While not attached, can be removed by the [[APS Turret]], nullifying its effects. This causes the turret to lose some health. {{Feature icon|Trigger on Impact|negative=true}} Does not trigger when thrown at a contestant, instead flies through them. ==== Charge ==== {{Feature icon|Attached}} Attaches to a surface upon deployment. Sticks to the surface even if it moves. Weighs down any [[Arena Carriables|carriable object]] it is attached to. {{Feature icon|Solid}} Has its own collision, albeit of a very small size, that can be stood upon. {{Feature icon|Arming Time}} Disarmed when initially deployed or while picked up as an attachment. Does not detect enemies while disarmed. Arms automatically after a wind-up time. {{Feature icon|Destructible}} Can be destroyed if its health is fully depleted, such as through hits from bullets or explosions. This causes the C4 to explode. Teammates can also destroy it. {{Feature icon|Glitchable}} Can be temporarily disabled by a [[Glitch Grenade]] or [[Glitch Barrel]]. {{Feature icon|Reshapeable}} Can be reshaped by the [[Data Reshaper]] into a piece of [[Arena Carriables|decor]] by opponents. {{Feature icon|Sound Cue}} Produces a constant beeping noise while it is armed, alerting nearby contestants of its presence. {{Feature icon|Permanent}} Does not disappear by itself. {{Feature icon|Reversible}} Can be used against the user's team, if an opponent triggers the explosion by destroying the gadget. Any damage and eliminations are attributed to the opponent. ==== Explosion ==== {{Feature icon|Explosive}} Deals damage in an area of effect that can be intercepted by structures and shields. {{Feature icon|Damaging}} Deals damage to contestants. {{Feature icon|Major Structure Damage}} Damages structures. Instantly destroys a concrete wall. {{Feature icon|Friendly Fire|negative=true}} Can damage the user, but not their teammates (unless an opponent caused it to explode). == Guide == === Strengths === * The C4 can be planted on or around a [[Cashout Station]] to defend it. When detonated, it will break the floor the Cashout Station is on and drop it to a floor below. ** A second C4 can be placed on the floor below the Cashout Station to force it to drop even further. This tactic is called a Double Drop. * The massive amounts of damage the C4 does means that if enemies are hit by it they are guaranteed to be very low on health. === Weaknesses === * The C4 has an arming time, and so cannot be used immediately in the middle of combat, rather requiring some sort of setup to be used for the purpose of damaging opponents. ** If the C4 is detonated before it is fully armed it will only deal a fraction of the full damage it can deal. * The C4 can be disabled by a nearby [[Glitch Grenade]] or [[Glitch Barrel]] triggering, or reshaped by the [[Data Reshaper]]. === Tactics === * When a C4 is planted on a [[Cashout Station]] to protect it, it is worth noting that the explosion will not deal damage if the C4 is on one side of the station and the target is on another side. ** Environmental damage does not have damage line-of-sight checks however, so knocking a Cashout Station over so the C4 is completely hidden from view can be used to force a surprise drop. * The C4 can be combined with other explosives such as [[Pyro Mine]]s or [[Barrels]] to do massive amounts of burst damage, with the manual detonation starting a chain reaction of multiple explosions. Make sure to place the explosives next to the C4 for maximum damage. {{EquipmentMastery|source1=Deploying the C4|xp1=0|source2=Triggering the C4|xp2=0|source3=Damage dealt to structures by the C4|xp3=0.008 × Damage Dealt|source4=Damage dealt to opponents by the C4|xp4=1 × Damage Dealt}} {{EquipmentCosmetics}} ==History== {| class="wikitable" !Patch!!

{{Infobox gadgets |image=Defibrillator.png |name=DEFIBRILLATOR |quote={{quote|text=When charged, can be used on fallen teammates' statues to revive them instantly}} |build=Medium |type=Utility |unlock=Medic |cooldown=45s |ammo=1 |damage=50 |duration=[[Defibrillator#Effects|Revive Sickness]] - 5s |healing=50% HP on Revive }} The [[Defibrillator]] is a [[Medium]] class gadget that can revive a downed teammate automatically instead of needing to do so manually. {{Infographic | infographic-class = right | display = image | Image = mov_m_defibrillator.gif }} == Usage == The Defibrillator can be selected as one of three [[Gadgets|gadgets]] of any [[Medium]] build loadout, except when competing in the [[Terminal Attack]] and [[Team Deathmatch]] gamemodes. Once equipped, holding the primary fire button will prepare an activation of the Defibrillator. Releasing the button will activate the gadget as long as a valid target is within range and the minimum charge duration of 1 second is met. {{Control scheme|gadget=Equip [[Defibrillator]]|primary-fire=Prepare defibrillation (Hold)
Activate (Release)}} == Stats == === Effects === The Defibrillator, once deployed, must be prepared for a brief moment before activation. The contestant using the gadget is required to be both facing and within a short distance of either a teammate's [[Revive Statue]] or an opposing contestant. When a Defibrillator is used on a [[Revive Statue]], it starts an uninterruptible revival process that requires no further action from the user. A hologram appears at the statue's location and gradually re-materializes during the revival. Once the process is complete: *The revived contestant returns with half of their Build's maximum HP. Light 75, Medium 125, Heavy 175. *They gain brief invulnerability. *They suffer temporary revive sickness, which prevents them from using their Specializations or Gadgets for 5 seconds after being revived. Alternatively, the Defibrillator can be activated on an opposing contestant to instantly deal 50 damage to them. === Properties === ==== Gadget ==== {{Feature icon|Targeted}} Can be activated while targeting a [[Revive Statue]] to revive it (or alternatively, an opponent to damage them). {{Feature icon|Single Charge}} Can be used once, then recharges automatically over the cooldown time. ==== Zap ==== {{Feature icon|Damaging}} Can be used on an opponent to deal some damage to them. {{Feature icon|Interceptible|negative=true}} Can not be removed by the [[APS Turret]]. ==== Effect ==== {{Feature icon|Support}} Applies a positive effect to teammates. {{Feature icon|Glitchable|negative=true}} Cannot be disabled by a [[Glitch Grenade]] or [[Glitch Barrel]], meaning the revive in progress will not be interrupted. {{Feature icon|Reshapeable|negative=true}} Cannot be reshaped by the [[Data Reshaper]]. == Guide == === Strengths === * The Defibrillator can revive teammates faster and without needing to do so manually past the initial activation. ** This allows contestants to fight, defend or assist with objectives while the revive is in progress, instead of remaining still for multiple seconds to perform a full revive. === Weaknesses === * Contestants revived by the Defibrillator are left at a disadvantage, with 50% their maximum HP and being unable to use Specializations or Gadgets for 5 seconds. *Opposing contestants can easily camp and kill a teammate being revived by the Defibrillator due to the obvious hologram, timing, and sound cues. The defibrillator revive also becomes a waste if both the user and their revived teammate die during and/or immediately after the revival. ** To prevent this, contestants who are reviving a teammate should try to remain in close proximity to them. This will allow the contestant performing the revive to try and protect them from enemy contestants. Alternatively, the [[Revive Statue]] can be moved to a safer location before using the Defibrillator. *Using the Defibrillator as a weapon is highly impractical. Not only is it slower and deals slightly less damage than a melee attack, the Defibrillator's cooldown is incurred once it damages an enemy, effectively wasting it. ===Tactics=== * It is the responsibility of the Defibrillator user to ensure that their teammate won't immediately die upon revival. Moving the teammate's [[Revive Statue]] away from enemies or providing cover with abilities such as [[Goo]], the [[APS Turret]], or the [[Guardian Turret]] can all but guarantee the odds of successful revives. * The Defibrillator is best used for mid-fight Revives, such as if a teammate dies early into a fight. * The [[Healing Beam]] makes an excellent pairing with the Defibrillator, as it can heal the revived contestant and make them battle-ready quicker. {{EquipmentMastery|source1=Teammate resurrected by the Defibrillator|xp1=150|source2=Damage dealt by the Defibrillator|xp2=0|source3=Opponent Eliminated by the Defibrillator|xp3=0}} {{EquipmentCosmetics}} == Trivia == {{quote|text=All but one contestant eliminated on The Boundless. This would be a perfect time to have equipped a defibrillator!|source=Scotty}} == History == {| class="wikitable" !Patch !!

{{Infobox gadgets |image=APS_Turret.png |name=APS TURRET |quote={{quote|text=Deployable that shoots down and destroys enemy projectiles}} |build=Medium |type=Defensive |unlock=Engineer |cooldownbar=Destroyed - '''30s'''
Picked up manually - '''5s'''
Picked up remotely - '''15s''' |health=175 |radius=3m }} The [[APS Turret]] ''('''A'''ctive '''P'''rotection '''S'''ystem '''Turret''')'' is a [[Medium]] class placeable gadget that intercepts projectiles such as grenades from opposing teams. {{Infographic|infographic-class= right|display= image|Image= mov_m_apsturret.gif}} == Usage== The APS Turret can be selected as one of three [[gadgets]] of any [[Medium]] build loadout. While the [[Multi-Device]] is held, an indicator will show a potential placement of the APS Turret as a blue hologram in front of the user. If the hologram is red, the gadget will not fit in the target location. Using the primary trigger, the placement can be confirmed to deploy the gadget. It can be deployed on any surface, including walls and ceilings. The gadget can also be retrieved to restore a charge, by interacting with it for a few moments while looking at it from up close. {{Control scheme|gadget=Equip [[APS Turret]]|primary-fire=Confirm placement (Tap)|interact=Retrieve deployed APS Turret (Hold)}} == Stats == === Effects=== The APS Turret can be deployed by placing it down on any surface. It starts working immediately. Any projectiles that enter its vicinity are intercepted and effectively deleted without allowing them to trigger their damage or other effects. Examples of such projectiles include the [[Frag Grenade]], the [[RPG-7]] and [[CL-40]] grenades. Certain small projectiles, including the [[Recurve Bow]]'s arrows, the [[Throwing Knives]] and the [[KS-23]]'s slug shots, as well as [[barrels]], will not be affected by the APS Turret. The gadget can be damaged only by opponents. Additionally, whenever the APS Turret removes a projectile, it loses 17% of total health, meaning it can remove 6 projectiles before being destroyed. The gadget has its own visible health bar. ===Properties=== ==== Gadget==== {{Feature icon|Placeable}} Can be placed attached to a surface. An indicator shows the exact target placement. {{Feature icon|Single Charge}} Can be used once, then recharges automatically over the cooldown time. {{Feature icon|Retrievable}} Can be picked up after being deployed to restore a charge. {{Feature icon|Deployment Limit}} One APS Turret can be deployed at a time. A new deployment causes the existing APS Turret to disappear. ==== Turret ==== {{Feature icon|Attached}} Attaches to a surface upon deployment. Sticks to the surface even if it moves. Weighs down any [[Arena Carriables|carriable object]] it is attached to. {{Feature icon|Solid}} Has its own collision, meaning it blocks bullets and contestants can stand on it. {{Feature icon|Destructible}} Can be destroyed if its health is fully depleted, such as through hits from bullets, or when losing health from removing projectiles. Has a health bar and cannot take damage from the user's team. {{Feature icon|Glitchable}} Can be temporarily disabled by a [[Glitch Grenade]] or [[Glitch Barrel]]. {{Feature icon|Reshapeable}} Can be reshaped by the [[Data Reshaper]] into a piece of [[Arena Carriables|decor]] by opponents. {{Feature icon|Sound Cue}} Produces a constant beep while idling, and a loud noise when intercepting projectiles, alerting nearby contestants of its presence. {{Feature icon|Permanent}} Does not disappear by itself. {{Feature icon|Arming Time|negative=true}} Starts working immediately upon deployment. Overhand Throw (Release)|secondary-fire=Prepare underhand throw (Hold)
Underhand Throw (Release)}} == Stats == === Effects === The Dome Shield can be deployed by throwing it as a grenade. On its first impact, a large spherical shield is formed around the projectile. A spherical shield persist around the projectile and moves with it. The shield blocks incoming fire and projectiles from opposing teams and blocks explosion damage, but it does not prevent contestants moving through and it does not block gunfire from you or your teammates. The Dome Shield will be destroyed if its health is depleted, either by damage from player or decay over time. Additionally, the projectile itself has a much smaller health pool and can be destroyed quickly by opponents, causing the shield to disappear. === Properties === ==== Gadget ==== {{Feature icon|Grenade}} Can be thrown like a grenade, meaning overhand or underhand. The [[Jump Pad]] is a [[Medium]] class placeable gadget that launches away any contestants and other objects that come into contact with it.
{{Infographic|infographic-class=right|display=image
 | Image = mov_m_jumppad.gif
}}
== Usage ==
The Jump Pad can be selected as one of three [[Gadgets|gadgets]] of any [[Medium]] build loadout.

While the gadget is held, an indicator will show a potential placement of the Jump Pad as a blue hologram in front of the user. If the hologram is red, the gadget will not fit in the target location. Using the primary trigger, the placement can be confirmed to deploy the gadget. It can be deployed on any surface, including walls and ceilings.

The gadget can also be retrieved to restore a charge, by interacting with it for a few moments while looking at it from up close.
{{Control scheme|gadget=Equip [[Jump Pad]]|primary-fire=Confirm placement <small>(Tap)</small>|interact=Retrieve deployed Jump Pad <small>(Hold)</small>}}
== Stats ==
=== Effects ===
The Jump Pad can be deployed by placing it on any nearby surface. Any contestants or objects that touch the active part of the Jump Pad will be launched. Opponents and teammates alike can damage the Jump Pad to destroy it.

The gadget can be placed in any orientation. It will always launch objects in the orientation it is facing. For example, a Jump Pad placed on a wall will push objects away from the wall.

The [[Cashout Station|cashout station]], [[barrels]], [[Cash Box|cash boxes]], and the [[Frag Grenade]] are all examples of objects that can be affected by the Jump Pad.

The Jump Pad is usually placed either on a floor to launch straight up, or on a sloped surface. A sloped Jump Pad will launch contestants far across the arena.

=== Properties ===
==== Gadget ====
{{Feature icon|Placeable}} Can be placed attached to a surface. An indicator shows the exact target placement.

{{Feature icon|Single Charge}} Can be used once, then recharges automatically over the cooldown time.

{{Feature icon|Retrievable}} Can be picked up after being deployed to restore a charge.

{{Feature icon|Deployment Limit}} One Jump Pad can be deployed at a time. A new deployment causes the existing Jump Pad to disappear.

==== Pad ====
{{Feature icon|Attached}} Attaches to a surface upon deployment. Sticks to the surface even if it moves. Weighs down any [[Arena Carriables|carriable object]] it is attached to.

{{Feature icon|Solid}} Has its own collision, meaning it blocks bullets and contestants can stand on it.

{{Feature icon|Destructible}} Can be destroyed if its health is fully depleted, such as through hits from bullets or explosions. Teammates can also destroy it.

{{Feature icon|Reshapeable}} Can be reshaped by the [[Data Reshaper]] into a piece of [[Arena Carriables|decor]] by opponents.

{{Feature icon|Usable by Opponents}} Can be used by opponents to their advantage.

{{Feature icon|Movement}} Provides a special mode of transport for contestants. Also causes projectiles and objects to bounce.

{{Feature icon|Arming Time|negative=true}} Starts working immediately upon deployment.

{{Feature icon|Glitchable|negative=true}} Cannot be disabled by a [[Glitch Grenade]] or [[Glitch Barrel]].

{{Feature icon|Permanent|negative=true}} Disappears by itself after enough time has passed.

== Guide ==
=== Strengths ===
* When placed on a slope at an angle, such as on a roof in [[Monaco]], the user can travel a very far horizontal distance. The distance travelled becomes extreme during the Low Gravity event.

=== Weaknesses ===
* The Jump Pad can be destroyed by nearby damage from any source. However, it has a lot of health compared to most gadgets.
* Poor placement of the Jump Pad can cause teammates to waste time and leave them out of position.
* There is a small amount of variance to the Jump Pad's launch angle, preventing objects from bouncing on them indefinitely.

=== Tactics ===
* Thrown gadgets, as well as the projectiles from the [[CL-40]] can be bounced off of a Jump Pad, which can be useful for shooting around a cover such as by placing it on the wall in a doorway. However, placing the Jump Pad can only be done from a short distance making it effective only as a defensive tool.
* Sprinting, sliding or [[Evasive Dash|dashing]] into a jump pad will give the user additional horizontal distance.
* Can be placed on top of [[Goo]] to create an angled launch.
