The [[Zipline]] is a [[Medium]] class placeable gadget that allows contestants to travel back and forth between two locations by riding a Zipline.
{{Infographic|infographic-class = right|display = image
 | Image = mov_m_zipline.gif
}}
== Usage ==

The Zipline can be selected as one of three [[Gadgets|gadgets]] of any [[Medium]] build loadout.

While the gadget is held, an indicator will show a potential placement of the Zipline as a blue hologram on the targeted surface. If the hologram is red, the gadget will not fit in the target location. Using the primary trigger, the placement can be confirmed to deploy the gadget. It can be deployed on any surface, including walls and ceilings.

To ride the Zipline, a contestant can interact with the cable while near it to start riding it. The looking direction determines in which direction they will move.
{{Control scheme|gadget=Equip [[Zipline]]|primary-fire=Confirm placement <small>(Tap)</small>|interact=Ride Zipline}}
== Stats ==
=== Effects ===
The Zipline can be deployed by placing it attached to a surface. Uniquely, the Zipline be placed from a very long distance, up to 40 meters away. It does not need to be placed horizontally and can be placed vertically if needed.

Once placed, it functions like the Ziplines that normally appear in the arena: contestants (teammates and opponents) can ride them in either direction. It can be damaged and destroyed like a regular Zipline, and will not disappear by itself until the user places a new Zipline or respawns.

Ziplines will not break if the surface it is attached to moves. It will only break if the ends of the Zipline lose line of sight. 
=== Properties ===
==== Gadget ====
{{Feature icon|Placeable}} Can be placed attached to a surface. An indicator shows the exact target placement.

{{Feature icon|Single Charge}} Can be used once, then recharges automatically over the cooldown time.

{{Feature icon|Deployment Limit}} One Zipline can be deployed at a time. A new deployment causes the existing Zipline to disappear.

{{Feature icon|Retrievable|negative=true}} Cannot be picked up after being deployed.

==== Zipline ====
{{Feature icon|Attached}} Attaches to a surface upon deployment. Sticks to the surface even if it moves. Weighs down any [[Arena Carriables|carriable object]] it is attached to.

{{Feature icon|Solid}} Has its own collision, meaning it blocks bullets and other objects.

{{Feature icon|Destructible}} Can be destroyed if its health is fully depleted, such as through hits from bullets or explosions. Teammates can also destroy it.

{{Feature icon|Permanent}} Does not disappear by itself.

{{Feature icon|Usable by Opponents}} Can be used by opponents to their advantage.

{{Feature icon|Movement}} Provides a special mode of transport for contestants.

{{Feature icon|Reshapeable|negative=true}} Cannot be reshaped by the [[Data Reshaper]].

== Guide ==
=== Strengths ===
* The Zipline can create paths where there were none before. Depending on the area, a lot of travel time can be saved by creating a new connection, such as between the top of the Mall and the roof of the Apartments in [[Seoul]].
* The Zipline's pole is difficult to take down with ranged attacks due to its small size and high health. 

=== Weaknesses ===
* Weapons with high environmental damage such as the [[CL-40]] and [[KS-23]] can destroy a Zipline with a single shot.
* 2 [[Quick Melee]] attacks will also destroy a Zipline. 

=== Tactics ===
* Upon respawning, placing down a Zipline early on (from a team spawn point towards the objective) can greatly benefit the team to reaching the objective faster.
** It should be noted that only one Zipline can be deployed per user.
* Ziplines can be used as a fast getaway in a pinch, however enemies will also be able to ride the Zipline too.
** This tactic can also be used to bait enemies into landing on an [[Explosive Mine]] placed at the end of a Zipline.

The [[Glitch Trap]] is a [[Medium]] class mounted gadget that continuously glitches opponents in its vicinity to disable their gadgets.
{{Infographic|infographic-class=right|display=image | Image = mov_m_glitchmine.gif}} 
== Usage ==
The Glitch Trap can be selected as one of three [[Gadgets|gadgets]] of any [[Medium]] build loadout.

The primary trigger can be used to toss the gadget a small distance. It will attach to the first surface it contacts and arm itself after a few moments.

The gadget can also be retrieved to restore a charge, by interacting with it for a few moments while looking at it from up close.

{{Control scheme|gadget=Equip [[Glitch Trap]]|primary-fire=Toss <small>(Tap)</small>|interact=Retrieve deployed Glitch Trap <small>(Hold)</small>}}
== Stats ==
=== Effects ===
The Glitch Trap can be deployed with a small throw to attach it to a nearby surface. The gadget will arm itself after a few moments. Any contestant that enters the 5 meter range of the Glitch Trap will be glitched, making them unable to use their [[gadgets]] and [[specializations]]. They will remain glitched for as long as they remain within its 5m range, and is also within its line of sight. The line of sight begins from the exact center of the trap. This means that a Glitch Trap that is placed on the corner of a wall may not be able to reach opponents well on one side of the corner.

The first time a target is glitched, their actions will be interrupted. For example, if they are [[Arena Carriables|carrying]] an object, they will drop it. The user also receives a sound cue to indicate someone has been glitched. A visual effect shows a line from the target to the gadget to let them know where they are being glitched from.

=== Properties ===
==== Gadget ====
{{Feature icon|Tossed}} Can be thrown out a short distance, after which it attaches to the first surface it hits.

{{Feature icon|Multiple Charges}} Can be used 2 times. When a charge is used, it automatically recharges over the cooldown time.

{{Feature icon|Retrievable}} Can be picked up after being deployed to restore a charge.

{{Feature icon|Deployment Limit}} 2 Glitch Traps can be deployed at a time. An excess deployment causes the oldest Glitch Trap to disappear.

==== Projectile ====
{{Feature icon|Projectile}} Gets affected by gravity and has a travel time. Once attached, the gadget is no longer a projectile.

{{Feature icon|Interceptible}} While not attached, can be removed by the [[APS Turret]], nullifying its effects. This causes the turret to lose some health.

{{Feature icon|Trigger on Impact|negative=true}} Does not trigger when thrown at a contestant, instead flies through them.

==== Trap ====
{{Feature icon|Attached}} Attaches to a surface upon deployment. Sticks to the surface even if it moves. Weighs down any [[Arena Carriables|carriable object]] it is attached to.

{{Feature icon|Solid}} Has its own collision, albeit of a very small size, that can be stood upon.

{{Feature icon|Arming Time}} Disarmed when initially deployed or while picked up as an attachment. Does not detect enemies while disarmed. Arms automatically after a wind-up time.

{{Feature icon|Glitchable}} Can be temporarily disabled by a [[Glitch Grenade]] or [[Glitch Barrel]].

{{Feature icon|Reshapeable}} Can be reshaped by the [[Data Reshaper]] into a piece of [[Arena Carriables|decor]] by opponents.

{{Feature icon|Sound Cue}} Produces a constant beeping noise while it is armed, alerting nearby contestants of its presence.

{{Feature icon|Permanent}} Does not disappear by itself.

==== Effect ====
{{Feature icon|Glitching}} Glitches affected contestants, making them unable to use gadgets and obfuscating their HUD. Also interrupts processes such as holding a [[Arena_Carriables#Objective_Carriables|Cash Box]] upon initial contact, but not thereafter.

{{Feature icon|Damaging|negative=true}} Does not inflict damage.

{{Feature icon|Immobilizing|negative=true}} Does not stop affected contestants from moving.

{{Feature icon|Disabling|negative=true}} Does not disabe glitchable gadgets.

{{Feature icon|Friendly Fire|negative=true}} Can affect neither the user nor their teammates.

== Guide ==
==== Strengths ====
* The Glitch Trap can be planted on or around a [[Cashout Station]] to defend it.

==== Weaknesses ====
* The Glitch Trap can be disabled by a nearby [[Glitch Grenade]] or [[Glitch Barrel]] triggering, or reshaped by the [[Data Reshaper]].

==== Tactics ====
* The Glitch Trap works well when placed at entrances, as it can catch a contestant off-guard and cause them and their teammates to retreat until their [[specializations]] and [[gadgets]] become accessible again. It is also useful to place them near [[Revive Statue|revive statues]] to disable [[Defibrillator|defibrillators]].
* A Glitch Trap on or near the [[Cashout Station]] will cause an approaching opponent to drop their held [[Cash Box]], and may also throw them off.
* Placing Glitch Traps on the ceiling works well, as this means they will not be destroyed by explosions, are more difficult to spot and destroy, and will have a better line of sight to their opponents compared to a Glitch Trap on the wall. 
** However, it should be noted that the area of effect is spherical, thereby reducing its effective range compared to a Glitch Trap on the floor.

The [[Barricade]] is a [[Heavy]] class placeable gadget that creates a strong wall to take cover behind.

== Usage ==

The Barricade can be selected as one of three [[Gadgets|gadgets]] of any [[Heavy]] build loadout.

While the gadget is held, an indicator will show a potential placement of the Barricade as a blue hologram in front of the user. If the hologram is red, the gadget will not fit in the target location. The secondary trigger can be used to rotate the placement hologram. Using the primary trigger, the placement can be confirmed to deploy the gadget. It can be only deployed on floors, not walls or ceilings.

The gadget can also be retrieved to restore a charge, by interacting with it for a few moments while looking at it from up close.
{{Control scheme|gadget=Equip [[Barricade]]|primary-fire=Confirm placement <small>(Tap)</small>|secondary-fire=Rotate placement <small>(Tap)</small>|interact=Retrieve deployed Barricade <small>(Hold)</small>}}
== Stats ==
=== Effects ===
The Barricade can be deployed by placing it down on a nearby floor. It will absorb damage like a regular structure. Opponents can destroy it by attacking it. Items that deal high structure damage will have an easier time removing a Barricade. 

The Barricade is made up of 5 panels placed in a horizontal line, with each panel having the same amount of health.
=== Properties ===
==== Gadget ====
{{Feature icon|Placeable}} Can be placed attached to a surface. An indicator shows the exact target placement.

{{Feature icon|Multiple Charges}} Can be used 2 times. When a charge is used, it automatically recharges over the cooldown time.

{{Feature icon|Retrievable}} Can be picked up after being deployed to restore a charge.

{{Feature icon|Deployment Limit}} 4 Barricades can be deployed at a time. An excess deployment causes the oldest Barricade to disappear.

==== Barricade ====
{{Feature icon|Attached}} Attaches to a surface upon deployment. Sticks to the surface even if it moves. Weighs down any [[Arena Carriables|carriable object]] it is attached to.

{{Feature icon|Solid}} Has its own collision, meaning it blocks bullets and contestants can stand on it.

{{Feature icon|Destructible}} Can be destroyed if its health is fully depleted, such as through hits from bullets or explosions. Teammates can also destroy it.

{{Feature icon|Reshapeable}} Can be reshaped by the [[Data Reshaper]] into a piece of [[Arena Carriables|decor]] by opponents.

{{Feature icon|Permanent}} Does not disappear by itself.

{{Feature icon|Usable by Opponents}} Can be used by opponents to their advantage.

== Guide ==
=== Strengths ===
* The Barricade has the highest amount of health out of any gadget per segment, let alone when adding up the health of every segment.
* A relatively high amount of Barricades can be placed compared to other gadgets, making it strong on [[Power Shift]].
* The Barricade places itself nearly instantly. Besides offering fast cover, with good reflexes and prediction abilities, it can be used to "parry" projectiles, such as an [[RPG-7]]'s rocket or the [[Lockbolt]]'s projectile.

=== Weaknesses ===
* The [[Pyro Grenade]] can be thrown at a Barricade, making it unusable as a proper barrier as anyone hiding behind it will burn.
* Explosions with high structure damage such as the [[RPG-7]] can immediately breach a Barricade.
* A [[Data Reshaper]] can simply reshape Barricades into [[Arena Carriables]].
* The [[KS-23]]'s slugs or [[Sledgehammer]]'s overhead swings high enviromental damage apply to the Barricade and its panels, allowing those weapons to easily take them down.

=== Tactics ===
* The Barricade can be combined with the [[MGL32]]. After placing a Barricade, the user can fire their grenades at the ceiling while the target cannot retaliate as the user is taking cover behind the Barricade.
* The Barricade can be pre-selected during a [[Charge 'N' Slam]], allowing the user to place it when they finish charging and provide near instant cover.

{{EquipmentMastery|source1=Deploying the Barricade|xp1=50|source2=Damage dealt to the Barricade by teammates|xp2=0|source3=Damage dealt to the Barricade by opponents
|xp3=0.35 x damage intercepted}}
{{EquipmentCosmetics}}

== Trivia ==
* In [[Update:9.0.0|Update 9.0.0]] an unintended change to the Barricade's placement mechanic was made. It allowed contestant to place barricade on any surface regardless obstacles in the way. This introduced a lot of bugs, including the one that allowed contestants to move big environment chuncks.
** The change was reverted in [[Update:9.1.1|Hotfix 9.1.1]].

Holding the primary trigger will prepare a high-velocity overhand throw. Holding the secondary trigger will prepare a low-velocity underhand throw. While preparing a throw, the gadget's trajectory is indicated up to the point where it triggers on impact. Overhand Throw (Release)|secondary-fire=Prepare underhand throw (Hold)
Underhand Throw (Release)}} == Stats == === Effects === The Anti-Gravity Cube can be thrown, and when it hits the ground, it creates a large cylindrical area (8 meters in diameter and 12 meters tall) that rises upwards from the gadget. This area moves along with the cube and can pass through surfaces. Contestants and objects inside this area will levitate and slowly rise upwards until they reach the maximum height of the gadget's range. Even the [[Cashout Station]] can be lifted and moved by this effect. === Properties === ==== Gadget ==== {{Feature icon|Grenade}} Can be thrown like a grenade, meaning overhand or underhand. The trajectory and impact point are shown as an indicator. {{Feature icon|Single Charge}} Can be used once, then recharges automatically over the cooldown time. {{Feature icon|Retrievable|negative=true}} Cannot be picked up after being deployed. ==== Projectile ==== {{Feature icon|Projectile}} Gets affected by gravity and has a travel time. {{Feature icon|Bounce}} Bounces away when the projectile collides with a surface or contestant. {{Feature icon|Trigger on Impact}} Can fly for any amount of time and triggers when the projectile collides with a surface or contestant. {{Feature icon|Interceptible}} Can be removed by the [[APS Turret]], nullifying its effects. This causes the turret to lose some health. {{Feature icon|Destructible}} Can be destroyed if its health is fully depleted, such as through hits from bullets or explosions. Teammates can also destroy it. {{Feature icon|Reshapeable}} Can be reshaped by the [[Data Reshaper]] into a piece of [[Arena Carriables|decor]] by opponents. {{Feature icon|Sound Cue}} Produces a sound whenever it teleports something, alerting nearby contestants. {{Feature icon|Usable by Opponents}} Can be used by opponents to their advantage. {{Feature icon|Movement}} Provides a special mode of transport for contestants. Also works for moving projectiles and objects. {{Feature icon|Damaging|negative=true}} Hitting a contestant directly with the projectile does not deal damage. {{Feature icon|Glitchable|negative=true}} Cannot be disabled by a [[Glitch Grenade]] or [[Glitch Barrel]]. {{Feature icon|Damaging|negative=true}} Does not inflict damage. == Guide == === Strengths === * The Anti-Gravity Cube can lift the [[Cashout Station]], making it easier to defend - or in some situations, easier to steal. * The Anti-Gravity Cube can slow down players that enter it's radius without significant momentum and make them easy-to-hit, floating targets. * The Anti-Gravity Cube's effect area can pass and affect targets through surfaces above the cube in range. * The Anti-Gravity Cube's effect area, although being a slow ascend, can help contestants reach elevated places. === Weaknesses === * The Anti-Gravity Cube does not have shielding, destructive or damaging properties compared to the majority of the [[Heavy]] archetype's other options. * The Strength of being able to make enemies easy-to-hit, floating targets can also apply to the contestant using it and their teammates themselves, should they misplace it. * The Anti-Gravity Cube only has 150 HP and so can be very quickly destroyed with majority of [[Weapons]]. It can also be reshaped by the [[Data Reshaper]] and destroyed by an [[APS Turret]]. * With the radius being only 4 meters wide, the active area is not particularly big, making inaccurate throws combined with the 28s cooldown quite punishing. === Tactics === * During offense, the Anti-Gravity Cube can lift a [[Cashout Station]] that is being defended by an enemy team from above which allows the contestant's team to maintain the height advantage, rather than having to push into the area from the same height or below it. ** [[C4]], the [[RPG-7]], [[Explosive Canister|Explosive Canisters]] and especially the [[KS-23]] with it's ability to damage and destroy the enviroment by simply shooting are great to utilise with the cube in order to create openings above the [[Cashout Station]], should it be in an enclosed area. * During defense preparation, the Anti-Gravity Cube can be used to lift the [[Cashout Station]] prematurely to put it into advantegous positions. For instance, together with Goo from a [[Goo Barrel]], [[Goo Grenade]] or [[Goo Gun]], it can be fixated at the ceiling of a room, preventing common tactics of safely dropping the station from a floor below. With enough [[Goo]], the Station could be fully encased in this elevated positon, making it even more difficult to reach quickly. * During active defense, the Anti-Gravity Cube can be used to great extent to stall steals. ** While an enemy contestant could continue stealing the [[Cashout Station]] while they're both being lifted, they will be in an even more helpless position as they won't be able to escape easily while continuously floating. ** Depending on the positions, the [[Cashout Station]] could continue to float up while the enemy contestant stealing gets stopped by parts of the ceiling and vice versa, breaking line of sight and stopping a steal. ** The Anti-Gravity Cube can be destroyed on purpose to make floating players and the cashout fall unexpectedly, potentially making the stealing contestant cancel their interaction. * When in an open area or with enough space, the Anti-Gravity Cube can be thrown behind enemy [[Barricade|Barricades]] and walls of [[Goo]], lifting enemy contestants in range out of their defenses, forcing them to be slow and exposed or reposition. * The effect area of the Anti-Gravity Cube can trap players in the ceilings of rooms if theyre caught on map geometry or other objects, forcing them to destroy the cube to get down or make use of certain [[Specializations]] or [[Gadgets]]. ** This can be utilised when being chased and is particularly effective against enemies with melee weapons. The contestant can throw the cube behind them in hallways or other enclosed areas with tight access like doorframes, windows and vents. This also applies to jumping from elevated areas and into holes. Since the enemy will be lifted up, they will likely have trouble following as they'll continuously be lifted trying to enter. Enemies with melee weapons will additionally not be able to shoot and destroy the cube without the help of their teammates or certain [[Specializations]] or [[Gadgets]]. * The Anti-Gravity Cube affects not only player movement and momentum, but also that of placeable or throwable [[Gadgets]]. For instance, throwing a [[C4]] through an active Anti-Gravity Cube's area will make it fly slightly further than usual. ** It also affects [[Revive Statue|Revive Statues]], which can stall an enemy revive. Alternatively, a [[Revive Statue]] can be used as a sort of "carrier" for placeable [[Gadgets]], particularly the [[C4]], to make it float to an elevated position before detonating it. {{EquipmentMastery|source1=Deploying the Anti-Gravity Cube|xp1=75|source2=Teammates utilizing the anti-gravity field (player included)|xp2=75|source3=Enemies utilizing the anti-gravity field|xp3=0|source4=Objects caught in the anti-gravity field|xp4=0}} {{EquipmentCosmetics}} == Trivia == * The Anti-Gravity Cube is the signature gadget of [[CNS|Ariad]] from [[CNS]]. ==History== {| class="wikitable" !Patch!!

Reload - 2.3s |ammo=1 |duration=7s |maxrange=6m |damage=5 |health=Anchor - 200}} [[Category: Sticky Gadgets]] The '''Lockbolt''' is a [[Builds#Heavy|Heavy]] class [[Gadgets|gadget]] that launches a device capable of limiting the movement of opponents it attaches to. {{Infographic|infographic-class = right|display = image | Image = mov_h_lockbolt.gif }} == Usage == The Lockbolt can be selected as one of three gadgets of any Heavy build loadout. The anchor has a delay between attaching and activating, accompanied by a visual and audio cue. When activated near enemy contestants, it deals 5 points of damage and limits the distance the affected enemies can travel. Anchors will also attach to objective objects, such as Cash Boxes and Cashout Stations. The Lockbolt anchor will affect any enemy within line-of-sight at the time of activation. The enemy sees the effect as red chains across the bottom of their screen, and all players see a hologram of a chain connecting the affected player to the anchor. Opponents can damage the Lockbolt anchor to destroy it. If the anchor does not have any valid targets during activation, the anchor disappears. The Lockbolt can be used on ceilings, walls, or objects. The chain hologram still shows when the affected enemy goes behind a wall or obstacle. === Properties === ==== Gadget ==== {{Feature icon|Placeable}} Can be attached to a surface. This causes the turret to lose some health. {{Feature icon|Stable Accuracy}} Does not experience any decreased accuracy when not "aiming down sight". {{Feature icon|Damaging|negative=true}} Hitting a contestant directly with the projectile does not deal damage. {{Feature icon|Destructible|negative=true}} Cannot be destroyed mid-air by receiving damage such as from bullets or explosions. ==== Anchor ==== {{Feature icon|Attached}} Attaches to a surface upon deployment. Sticks to the surface even if it moves. {{Feature icon|Destructible}} Can be destroyed if its health is fully depleted, such as through hits from bullets or explosions. Cannot be destroyed by teammates. {{Feature icon|Reshapeable}} Can be reshaped by the [[Data Reshaper]] into a piece of [[Arena Carriables|decor]] by opponents. {{Feature icon|Arming Time}} Activates 2 seconds after deployment. {{Feature icon|Glitchable}} Can be disabled by a [[Glitch Grenade]] or [[Glitch Barrel]]. {{Feature icon|Damaging}} Deals damage to enemy contestants attached. {{Feature icon|Solid|negative=true}} Does not have its own collision, meaning it cannot blocks bullets and contestants cannot stand on it. {{Feature icon|Permanent|negative=true}} The effect disappears after some time or if there are no valid targets within its area of effect. == Guide == === Strengths === * Counters mobility of Light and Medium classes to make up for Heavy's lack of mobility. * Gives a visual cue for the direction of an enemy when they go behind obstacles. === Weaknesses === * The Lockbolt anchor can be destroyed, but it has decent health. * The deployment time gives the enemy some time to escape its area of effect. === Tactics === * Shooting the Lockbolt near a jump pad or zipline over a gap can cause the enemy to fall into the gap. * It can be used to delay the enemy in reaching the objective. * Lockbolt anchors will tether to objectives, such as Cash Boxes and Cashout Stations. This can be used to deny objectives to enemy teams, as it will only restrict enemy contestants from carrying Cash Boxes that are tethered. *Shooting a lockbolt onto an [[Goo Barrel]] or other [[Arena Carriables]] and then moving with the object can allow contestants to drag cashout stations to a location that favours their team. {{EquipmentMastery|source1=Deploying the Lockbolt|xp1=50|source2=Locking Enemies or Objects|xp2=25 per Contestant Locked}} {{EquipmentCosmetics}} == History == {| class="wikitable" !Patch !!

The '''Breach Drill''' is a [[Medium]] class gadget that can be attached to a surface to flash the other side before detonating to breach it.
{{Infographic
 | infographic-class = right
 | display = image
 | Image = mov_m_breach_drill.gif
}} 
==Usage==
The Breach Drill can be selected as one of three [[Gadgets]] of any [[Medium]] build loadout.

Once attached to a surface, the Breach Drill will begin drilling through. When completed, a flash will blind opponents on the other side, followed by an explosion that destroys the targeted surface.

Fully blinding an opponent will display a yellow X on the crooshair, while partially blinding displays a white one.

Breach drill can be placed on top of [[Goo]]. The explosion breaks a single goo piece, but the flash doesn't blind any opponents.
{{Control scheme
|gadget=Equip [[Breach Drill]]
|primary-fire=Place
}}

=== Properties ===
==== Gadget ====
{{Feature icon|Placeable}} Can be placed attached to a surface. An indicator shows the exact target placement.

{{Feature icon|Multiple Charges|negative=true}} Can be used once. When a charge is used, it automatically recharges over the cooldown time.

{{Feature icon|Retrievable|negative=true}} Can't be picked up after being deployed to restore a charge.

==== Drill ====
{{Feature icon|Attached}} Attaches to a surface upon deployment. Sticks to the surface even if it moves. Can't be attatched to [[Arena Carriables|carriable object]]s.

{{Feature icon|Solid}} Has its own collision that can be stood upon.

{{Feature icon|Trigger on Time}} Triggers after a fixed amount of time. Drills through the wall for 2 seconds, then flashes the enemies and after 0.5 seconds breaks the wall.

{{Feature icon|Reshapeable}} Can be reshaped by the [[Data Reshaper]] into a piece of [[Arena Carriables|decor]] by opponents.

{{Feature icon|Sound Cue}} Produces an audible drilling noise before going off.

{{Feature icon|Glitchable|negative=true}} Can't be temporarily disabled by a [[Glitch Grenade]] or [[Glitch Barrel]].

{{Feature icon|Destructible|negative=true}} Can't be destroyed by receiving damage. 

{{Feature icon|Permanent|negative=true}} Disappears after destroying the wall.

==== Flash ====
{{Feature icon|Visibility}} Affects the line of sight of the user and/or opponents. Anyone looking at the Breach Drill when it triggers will be temporarily blinded.

{{Feature icon|Friendly Fire}} Can affect both the user and their teammates.

{{Feature icon|Damaging|negative=true}} Does not deal damage to contestants. 

{{Feature icon|Immobilizing|negative=true}} Does not stop affected contestants from moving.

==== Explosion ====
{{Feature icon|Major Structure Damage}} Damages structures. Instantly destroys a concrete wall.

{{Feature icon|Damaging}} Deals damage to the user and/or opponents at point blank rage.

==Guide==

===Strengths===
*[[Breach Drill]] is a multipurpose gadget that can simultaneously function in the same roles as the [[Dematerializer]] and [[Flashbang]].
*[[Breach Drill]] is one of the few arena destruction tools available to [[Builds#Medium_Build|Medium build]] contestants.
*It can trigger other explosives [[Category:Sticky_Gadgets|Sticky Gadgets]], if they’re in close proximity to its explosion.
*The Drill is a physical object that blocks paths and bullets and can be climbed. It also means it can fall to the ground if the wall is destroyed or [[Dematerializer|dematerialized]].
*Due to it being placed directly on surfaces rather than thrown, it lends itself to plays requiring precise placement of explosives or flashbangs.

===Weaknesses===
*While the gadget can serve as a replacement for the [[Dematerializer]] and [[Flashbang]], it has only one charge and a longer cooldown than either of them.
*Blinding from the Breach Drill is not unidirectional. It works the same way as a [[Flashbang]], so if contestants break or [[Dematerializer|dematerialize]] the wall, it will flash everyone in the line of sight.
*Due to the controlled nature of the detonation, the destructive potential of the drill is lesser than options such as [[Explosive Canister]]s.
*The sound of the drill is audible from the opposite side of the wall, giving enemies a warning prior to the flashbang and detonation.

===Tactics===
*[[Breach Drill]] is a very effective tool for closed spaces. It shines the most in buildings or areas with a lot of cover, both for its blinding and destructive capabilities. But due to its single charge, long cooldown, and limited usefulness in open areas, it can be more situational than other loadout options.
*The short detonation time allows for impromptu use in deterring attackers: it can be used to quickly create gaps between the user and melee users, or blind attackers pursuing players attempting to retreat into structures.
*While it isn’t as strong as the other available options, the versatile nature of the Breach Drill means contestants can use it in creative ways:
**The Breach Drill can complement teams focused on close range fights; particularly with [[:Category:Melee|Melee weapons]] like the [[Riot Shield]], as it can block the blinding from the drill.
**It’s helpful for denying cashout steals from beneath the cashboxes, especially when paired with certain types of [[Mines]].

The [[Explosive Mine]] is a [[Medium]] or [[Heavy]] class mounted gadget which, when it comes into contact with an opponent or when it is destroyed, creates an explosion that deals high damage.

== Usage ==
The Explosive Mine can be selected as one of three [[Gadgets|gadgets]] of any [[Medium]] or [[Heavy]] build load-out.

The primary trigger can be used to toss the gadget a small distance. It will attach to the first surface it contacts and arm itself after a few moments(2.0 seconds after primary mouse click).

The gadget can also be retrieved to restore a charge, by interacting with it for a few moments while looking at it from up close.
{{Control scheme|gadget=Equip [[Explosive Mine]]|primary-fire=Toss <small>(Tap)</small>|interact=Retrieve deployed Explosive Mine <small>(Hold)</small>}}
== Stats ==
=== Effects ===
The Explosive Mine can be deployed with a small throw to attach it to a nearby surface. The gadget will arm itself after a few moments. If an opponent gets too close to the Explosive Mine, or if it is destroyed such as by bullets or by a nearby explosion, it explodes, dealing high damage to nearby opponents and damaging structures. It also damages the user if they are too close.

If an opponent destroys the gadget, they become the user instead, meaning any damage it deals is attributed to them.

=== Properties ===
==== Gadget ====
{{Feature icon|Tossed}} Can be thrown out a short distance, after which it attaches to the first surface it hits.

{{Feature icon|Retrievable}} Can be picked up after being deployed to restore a charge.

{{Feature icon|Deployment Limit}} 2 Explosive Mines can be deployed at a time. An excess deployment causes the oldest Explosive Mine to disappear.

==== Projectile ====
{{Feature icon|Projectile}} Gets affected by gravity and has a travel time. Once attached, the gadget is no longer a projectile.

{{Feature icon|Interceptible}} While not attached, can be removed by the [[APS Turret]], nullifying its effects. This causes the turret to lose some health.

{{Feature icon|Trigger on Impact|negative=true}} Does not trigger when thrown at a contestant, instead flies through them.

==== Mine ====
{{Feature icon|Attached}} Attaches to a surface upon deployment. Sticks to the surface even if it moves. Weighs down any [[Arena Carriables|carriable object]] it is attached to.

{{Feature icon|Solid}} Has its own collision, albeit of a very small size, that can be stood upon.

{{Feature icon|Arming Time}} Disarmed when initially deployed or while picked up as an attachment. Does not detect enemies while disarmed. Arms automatically after a wind-up time.

{{Feature icon|Destructible}} Can be destroyed if its health is fully depleted, such as through hits from bullets or explosions. This causes the Explosive Mine to explode. Teammates can also destroy it.

{{Feature icon|Glitchable}} Can be temporarily disabled by a [[Glitch Grenade]] or [[Glitch Barrel]].

{{Feature icon|Reshapeable}} Can be reshaped by the [[Data Reshaper]] into a piece of [[Arena Carriables|decor]] by opponents.

{{Feature icon|Sound Cue}} Produces a constant beeping noise while it is armed, alerting nearby contestants of its presence.

{{Feature icon|Permanent}} Does not disappear by itself.

{{Feature icon|Reversible}} Can be used against the user's team, if an opponent triggers the explosion by destroying the gadget. Any damage and eliminations are attributed to the opponent.

==== Explosion ====

{{Feature icon|Explosive}} Deals damage in an area of effect that can be intercepted by structures and shields.

{{Feature icon|Damaging}} Deals damage to contestants.

{{Feature icon|Moderate Structure Damage}} Damages structures. Takes a few seconds or multiple charges to break a concrete wall.

{{Feature icon|Friendly Fire|negative=true}} Can damage the user, but not their teammates (unless an opponent caused it to explode).

== Guide ==
=== Strengths ===
* The Explosive Mine can be planted on or around a [[Cashout Station]] to defend it.
* The Explosive Mine deals significant damage, itself being capable of almost eliminating a [[Light]] contestant, leaving them at 30 HP.
* The Explosive Mine doesn't require remote activation. This means the contestant using it doesn't need to surveillance the Mine to activate it at the right moment. Not requiring remote activation also allows it to potentially eliminate enemies even after the contestant using it has been eliminated and is waiting to respawn.

=== Weaknesses ===
* The Explosive Mine can be disabled by a nearby [[Glitch Grenade]] or [[Glitch Barrel]] triggering, or reshaped by the [[Data Reshaper]].
* Compared to the [[Gas Mine]] and [[Pyro Mine]], a contestant can only have one Explosive Mine charge available at any time.
** Two Explosive Mines can still simultaneously be placed in the enviroment by the same contestant.

=== Tactics ===
* Explosive Mines are best placed in spots where enemy contestants are likely to pass through without looking or checking carefully, like: behind closed doors, around corners, below or above windows, etc.
* The Explosive Mine combines well with certain [[Weapons]], [[Gadgets]] and specifically the [[Oil Barrel]].
** While all weaponry can manually trigger it by shooting, doing so with the [[CL-40]] will stack it's damage on top of the Explosive Mine's damage, which can instantly eliminate a [[Light]] contestant if the [[CL-40|CL-40's]] projectile is close enough.
*** Although the same can be done with the [[MGL32]], it is more difficult due to the weapon's projectiles not exploding on first impact.
** Besides exploding on enemy contact or when being shot, the Explosive Mine can also be manually detonated with other explosive gadgets such as [[Breach Charge|Breach Charges]], [[C4]] and the [[RPG-7]]. These can be utilised together with the Explosive Mine to create stronger, more damaging explosions. 
*** With the [[RPG-7]] specifically it can be used to make a very quick trap in a dire situation for when the contestant is being chased by one or multiple opponents, as the contestant only needs to wait for the Explosive Mine to arm. 
** A [[Gas Mine]] in combination with the Explosive Mine will instantly eliminate a [[Light]] contestant and spread toxic gas in the area around their [[Revive Statue]], making a revive on the spot very difficult for the time being and still dealing some damage when the statue is being picked up and carried elsewhere while the gas is still present.
** The [[Oil Barrel]] in combination with the Explosive Mine deals so much additional damage that it can near instantly eliminate a [[Medium]] contestant without the need of another gadget or the contestant's weapon. Unless they get healed quickly upon stepping into the trap, they will succumb to the fire damage, usually within a second or less depending on the proximity to the barrel's explosion. Additionally, this causes fire to spread around the [[Revive Statue]] which will result in the same negative effects for that contestant's team as the aforementioned [[Gas Mine]] combination.
*** The same strategy can be applied or extended with [[Glitch Barrel|Glitch Barrels]], which will prevent the use of any [[Specializations]] or [[Gadgets]], including those that could heal the victims or give them extra mobility to escape the trap.
*** Note that the [[Explosive Canister]] is not well suited for this, as the explosion from the Mine will not make the Canister explode immediately and instead make it tumble through the enviroment unpredictably for a moment.
*** For the same strategy to work with the [[Gas Canister]], two Explosive Mines are required, as the explosion of a single one is not enough to trigger the Canister.
* The Explosive Mine can act as an improvised [[Breach Charge]], although a concrete wall will require multiple mines to breach. 
** However, the enviromental damage is enough for one mine to destroy [[Goo]] within the radius. This can be useful for quickly getting rid of walls of [[Goo]] created through [[Goo Barrel|Goo Barrels]] or the [[Goo Grenade]] without the need of repeatedly shooting it with the contestant's main weapon.
*While a very niche tactic, the Explosive Mine can be immediately detonated through the use of a [[Quick Melee]] attack right when the contestant throws it, creating a close-range explosion.

The [[Proximity Sensor]] is a [[Medium]] and [[Heavy]] class mounted gadget that continuously reveals the location of opponents in its line of sight to the user's team.
{{Infographic|infographic-class = right|display = image
 | Image = mov_h_motionsensor.gif
}} 
== Usage ==
The Proximity Sensor can be selected as one of three [[Gadgets|gadgets]] of any [[Medium]] or [[Heavy]] build loadout.

The primary trigger can be used to toss the gadget a small distance. It will attach to the first surface it contacts and will start working immediately.

The gadget can also be retrieved to restore a charge, by interacting with it for a few moments while looking at it from up close.
{{Control scheme|gadget=Equip [[Proximity Sensor]]|primary-fire=Toss <small>(Tap)</small>|interact=Retrieve deployed Proximity Sensor <small>(Hold)</small>}}
== Stats ==
=== Effects ===
The Proximity Sensor can be deployed with a small throw to attach it to a nearby surface. Whenever a contestant comes close, the Proximity Sensor will detect them, revealing their location to the user's team as long as they remain in range.

The user's team can see the opponent in the form of particles in the shape of their body in the color of their team, which are visible regardless of distance or any surfaces between the target and the viewer. 

The target has a warning on their screen that they are detected, and a visual effect shows a line from the target to the gadget to let them know where it is.
=== Properties ===
==== Gadget ====
{{Feature icon|Tossed}} Can be thrown out a short distance, after which it attaches to the first surface it hits.

{{Feature icon|Multiple Charges}} Can be used 2 times. When a charge is used, it automatically recharges over the cooldown time.

{{Feature icon|Retrievable}} Can be picked up after being deployed to restore a charge.

{{Feature icon|Deployment Limit}} 2 Proximity Sensors can be deployed at a time. An excess deployment causes the oldest Proximity Sensor to disappear.

==== Projectile ====
{{Feature icon|Projectile}} Gets affected by gravity and has a travel time. Once attached, the gadget is no longer a projectile.

{{Feature icon|Interceptible}} While not attached, can be removed by the [[APS Turret]], nullifying its effects. This causes the turret to lose some health.

==== Sensor ====
{{Feature icon|Attached}} Attaches to a surface upon deployment. Sticks to the surface even if it moves. Weighs down any [[Arena Carriables|carriable object]] it is attached to.

{{Feature icon|Solid}} Has its own collision, albeit of a very small size, that can be stood upon.

{{Feature icon|Destructible}} Can be destroyed if its health is fully depleted, such as through hits from bullets or explosions. Teammates can also destroy it.

{{Feature icon|Glitchable}} Can be temporarily disabled by a [[Glitch Grenade]] or [[Glitch Barrel]].

{{Feature icon|Reshapeable}} Can be reshaped by the [[Data Reshaper]] into a piece of [[Arena Carriables|decor]] by opponents.

{{Feature icon|Sound Cue}} Plays a sound to alert the user's team when it detects something.

{{Feature icon|Permanent}} Does not disappear by itself.

{{Feature icon|Detecting}} Reveals the position of affected contestants to the user's team. The detection is visible through walls. A warning is shown to detected contestants.

{{Feature icon|Arming Time|negative=true}} Starts working immediately upon deployment. Remains armed while picked up as an attachment.

{{Feature icon|Damaging|negative=true}} Does not inflict damage.

== Guide ==
=== Strengths ===
* The Proximity Sensor can protect the user's team by covering sightlines that they are not holding at the moment.
* Placing the sensor on the inside of a doorway can help prevent its destruction by enemies, who are forced to either reveal themselves or avoid the path entirely.

=== Weaknesses ===
* If placed in a location where it is easily noticeable from a distance, the Proximity Sensor can be shot down before being able to detect the opponent.
* The Proximity Sensor can be disabled by a nearby [[Glitch Grenade]] or [[Glitch Barrel]] triggering, or reshaped by the [[Data Reshaper]].
